# A Friend’s Brief Report Concerning Elias

...and just as he is distinguished from all other men in his teaching, so he is also quite unique in his temperament <term>Gemüthsart<note>This refers to one's natural disposition or character.</note></term>, in the way he combines severity and a kindly nature. This can be compared to nothing better than the great severity and great mercy of God in His judgment. He is entirely removed from all outward, affected sanctity or hypocrisy. His primary principle is that a person must not present themselves outwardly as anything other than what they are in fact. All hypocrisy would be an abomination before God. One should keep the good in secret, and God, who sees into what is hidden, will reward it openly; for man shall be judged solely according to the inner ground of the heart <term>Herzensgrund<note>A term common in German Pietism and mysticism, referring to the deepest, most authentic core of a person’s soul where they interact with God.</note></term>. This is how he has been found to be, both in personal interactions held with him a few years ago and through his writings, which one has occasionally had the opportunity to read.

### In the Year 1772.

<note>The name **Elias** is the Greek and Latin form of the Hebrew name **Elijah**. In 18th-century mystical and pietistic circles, Elijah was often invoked as a figure who would return to resolve all religious disputes and usher in a unified, "true" understanding of scripture.</note>

<term>Talmud<note>The central text of Rabbinic Judaism, consisting of the Mishnah (oral law) and the Gemara (commentary). The author here claims to present its "true sense," likely suggesting an interpretation that moves away from strict legalism toward a more universal or spiritual philosophy.</note></term>

<term>Rabbis<note>Original: "Rabbinen." Refers to the Jewish sages and teachers whose interpretations form the basis of the Talmud.</note></term>

<note>The phrase **Gathering of all Peoples into one single faith** reflects the 18th-century Enlightenment and mystical ideal of religious universalism—the hope that through reason or spiritual revelation, all divisions between religions would disappear in favor of a shared belief in a single Creator.</note>

<summary>This is the title page of a 1772 manuscript that seeks to harmonize the teachings of the Talmud and the Rabbis with a universal monotheism intended to unite all humanity.</summary>

# A Short Report from a Friend about Elias.

...and just as he is distinguished from all other people in his teaching, so he is also quite unique in his temperament, combining severity and a kind nature. This can be compared to nothing better than the great severity and great mercy of God in His judgment. He is entirely removed from all outward, affected holiness or hypocrisy <note>The original German uses *Scheinheiligkeit*, literally "shining-holiness," referring to a false or performative piety.</note>. His fundamental principle is that a person must not present themselves outwardly as anything other than what they truly are in reality. All hypocrisy is an abomination before God. One should keep good deeds in secret, and God, who sees into what is hidden, will reward them openly; for man shall be judged solely according to the inner depths of the heart <term>Herzensgrund: a term common in German mysticism and Pietism referring to the deepest, most authentic core of a person’s soul where they meet God.</term>. This is how he has been found, both in personal interactions with him a few years ago, and from his writings which one has occasionally had the opportunity to read.

## Preface.

The **Rabbinic books** and the entire <term>Talmud</term> <note>The central text of Rabbinic Judaism, consisting of the Mishnah (legal traditions) and the Gemara (commentaries).</note> are God's own word, which he has written with his own hand. This I wish only to mention here as a reminder beforehand, rather than proving it at great length, because such a thing is already firmly proven in the "Book of the Whole World" <note>This likely refers to a specific contemporary theological work or the concept of the "Book of Nature/History" as a witness to divine truth.</note>; and also because the actual content of these books proves sufficiently by itself that they are God’s own word, and not the word of men. God says in **Isaiah 46:9**: *I am God, and there is none else, a God like whom there is none elsewhere. I who announce beforehand what shall come hereafter, and beforehand, even before it happens, and say: my <term>counsel</term> <note>Original: "Anschlag." In this context, it refers to a divine plan, purpose, or decree.</note> stands, and I do everything that pleases me.* Likewise in **Chapter 48:3**: *I have announced it beforehand, this future thing; it has flowed from my mouth, and I have had it spoken. I also act suddenly, so that it comes to pass. I announced it to you beforehand, and had it told to you before it came, so that you might not say: my image and idol does it, and has commanded it.*

It is God alone, therefore, who can reveal and describe the future; the Talmud and the Rabbis, however, have [known] everything

# Preface.

God of all nations, who is also at the same time the first ancestor <note>original: "Stammvater"</note> of all nations, Adam; but not the disobedient, sinful Adam, for that is a different one, as will be seen in this book. # Chapter 1.

## The 13 Articles of Faith of Israel.

->§. I.<-

<image-desc>A decorative square woodcut initial 'D' featuring a central shield with a bird, surrounded by dense foliate ornament.</image-desc>The 13 Articles of Faith of the people of Israel were written by God under the name of *Rabbi Moshe ben Maimon*, who is also called *Rambam*. *Rambam* is named after the initial letters of his name, as in the *R* from *Rabbi*, the *M* from *Moshe*, and so forth. <note>This refers to the common Hebrew practice of creating acronyms for famous scholars; Maimonides is widely known as the Rambam (Rabbi Moses ben Maimon).</note> He is described as a physician to King *Saladin* in *Egypt*, and he represents the Messiah as he is still present in the *Egypt* of this time, and in the external church and doctrine, bringing the doctrine of the Word of God into its true principles and articles. <note>The author uses "Egypt" and "Saladin" allegorically to represent the spiritual bondage or external state of the contemporary world where the Messiah is secretly at work.</note> The 13 Articles signify the 13 years that God gave to the Messiah to organize this doctrine in the *Revelation of Christ* <note>original: "O. C." or "Offenbarung Christi"</note> into its proper order, before it was to go forth publicly into the Church. He is said to have been born around the year of the world 4891, which is the year of Christ 1049, <note>The author's dates differ significantly from the historical dates of Maimonides (c. 1135–1204), reflecting the esoteric chronological system established in the preface.</note> specifically on the eve of Passover in *Cordoba* in *Spain*, at 3 o'clock in the afternoon: and he is said to have died in the 75th year of his age, in the year of the world 4965, which is the year of Christ 1123, in the Promised Land, according to the book

<page-num>10</page-num>
<header>The 13 Articles of Faith</header>

*Shalshelet* <note>original: "Schalschelet," referring to the *Shalshelet Ha-Kabbalah* or "Chain of Tradition," a 16th-century history of the Jewish people</note> page 44; but in Egypt, according to Samuel Shullam, in the book *Juchasin* <note>original: "Sefer Yuchasin," or "Book of Lineage," a historical work by Abraham Zacuto</note> page 131. See also Wolf’s *Bibliotheca Hebraica* Part I, page 834.

The 75 years are one and the same with the 75 years of Abraham when he departed from the land of idols, Chaldea (Genesis 12:5). This represents the departure of the Messiah from the external teaching of the letter into the true teaching of the Word of God. Here, he dies to the external teaching, and this is the "Death of Maimonides." His birth, however, is the resurrection and the becoming-alive in the true doctrine. And because this teaching facilitates the transition from this current time and from the external doctrine into the Kingdom of the Messiah—which is the Passover and the exodus from the "Egypt" of this era—his birth is placed on Easter Eve. Three o’clock in the afternoon is the 9th hour of the day and the end of Christ’s crucifixion; it signifies the end of this current age and the external Church, now that Christ has been crucified enough. That his birth is placed in Spain signifies that the Messiah is from among the Christians. The year-date here is meant to signify nothing more than the late period in which the books of the Rabbis were published and became known as the final form of the Word of God. For there are six kinds of the Word of God:

1. The books of the Heathen Church under the doctrine of the gods;
2. The O.T. or Old Testament;
3. The N.T. or New Testament;
4. The Talmud together with the Targum <note>Aramaic translations/interpretations of the Hebrew Bible</note> and Masora <note>The traditional system of notes on the biblical text</note>;
5. The Alcoran <note>The Quran</note> of the Mohammedan Church;
6. And finally, the books of the Rabbis, which were the last to come forth and serve specifically to explain the two Testaments as the primary foundation of the entire Church.

Under the aforementioned name *Rambam*, the book *Thirteen Articles of Faith* <note>original Hebrew: *Sheloš 'eśrē 'iqqārîm* (עשרה עקרים שלש), often called the *Thirteen Principles*</note>, or the 13 Roots or Foundations, * as it is properly called, was written. In the same way, this doctrine of the Word of God in the Revelation of C. <note>Possibly referring to the "Revelation of Christ" or a specific sect's manuscript.</note> is unique among all peoples, and such a unity does not exist apart from it among all the doctrines of all external religions. The doctrines of the Word of God are also called Elohim, and are many in the letter [of the text], but one in the true sense. All the Word of God among all peoples resolves itself into a single sense, and all other doctrines must bow beneath it. It reveals to all nations the one God, their ancestor, from whom they all descend, and who was hidden from everyone until now, according to the words of Isaiah 45:15: *Truly, you are a hidden God, you God of Israel, you Savior.* But of the Messiah he says in Psalm 91:14: *He knows my name, therefore I will help him.*

# The 13 Articles of Faith.

And of the whole Israel of the faithful among all nations he says regarding this present time: *Therefore my people shall know my name, at that same time*, Isaiah 52:6. These words indisputably refer to the end times. If his name is only then to be recognized there, it follows naturally that it was previously unknown to all nations. Now it is revealed, therefore: *Hear, Israel, Jehovah, our Elohim <note>Hebrew: אלהים; a name for God denoting power and judgment, often used alongside the personal name Jehovah.</note>, is one Jehovah!*

## The III. Article.

§. 5. I believe with perfect faith that the Creator, whose name be blessed, is not a physical being, that physical things do not affect him, and that he has no likeness whatsoever.

In this regard, Maimon <note>Refers to Moses Maimonides (1138–1204), the philosopher whose "13 Principles" form the basis of this text.</note> cites the words from Deuteronomy 4:15: 
> "Take good heed therefore unto your souls; for ye saw no manner of similitude on the day that Jehovah spake unto you in Horeb out of the midst of the fire."

In this view, God is the spiritual nature of the world, and not the personal God. This God is spread everywhere throughout the whole world, and is also in the body of a mother and forms the child, without being affected by the physical substance or the filth <note>The author uses "Koth" (filth/excrement) to emphasize that God’s purity is not compromised by the messy realities of biological life.</note>. In this sense, he is power, life, and spirit, which dwells within all things, and yet nothing affects him. But the personal God is nonetheless the Lord over all of that, just as the intellect in man, which has its primary seat in the head, rules and governs all the powers of the entire body. 

Thus, when we pray to the personal God that he might rule us through his Spirit, we pray that he might rule us through this spiritual being which is spread throughout the whole world, and which lies hidden within the inner part of the outer nature of the world, like the soul in the body. This is the Spirit of God, which the personal God governs, just as a man governs his own spirit. This, his imperishable spirit, is in all things, Wisdom of Solomon 12:1, but a malicious external nature of a man does not affect him. He does not enter into a malicious soul, and the natural man does not perceive the things that are of the Spirit of God, 1 Corinthians 2:14. He flees from the idolatrous priests of Baal <note>original: "Baals-Pfaffen"; a derogatory term for priests, used here to criticize those the author deems spiritually blind or idolatrous.</note>, Wisdom of Solomon 1:5. For they are the stiff-necked who always resist the Holy Spirit, Acts 7:51. 

The same Spirit bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God, Romans 8:16, and his characteristic sign is love, mercy, compassion, charity toward the poor and needy, humility, and gentleness. One must taste and feel this spiritual being of the Godhead, otherwise one cannot form an image or likeness of it, for it has no physical form. Therefore, when God's word tells us that we should not make for ourselves any image of God ma—

This article is thus set in opposition to the priestly delusion <note>original: *Pfaffenteufel*, literally "priest-devil," a derogatory term used by radical reformers to describe orthodox dogmas they believed were deceptive or "devilish" inventions of the clergy.</note> of the Christians, which has made a separate person out of the Father, and also a separate person out of the Spirit. ### The V. Article.

§. 7. **I believe with perfect faith that the Creator, whose name be blessed, alone is worthy to be worshiped, and that besides him no one is worthy of worship.**

There are high angels who serve the governance of the world, and all the primary natures of the world, together with all the stars, work together in the creation of things on Earth. But they all stand beneath the personal God, and he has created them all. Therefore, he alone is worthy of worship, and no angel, nor spirit, nor any creature; and the Father shall be honored and worshiped in the Son, for the Father is in the Son and the Son in the Father and both are one. To the personal God all power and authority has been given, and he is our **Father Adam** <note>This refers to the "Heavenly Adam" or *Adam Kadmon*, a mystical concept where the first human is seen as the divine archetype or the "Personal God" through whom the infinite Spirit acts.</note>; therefore our spirit and mind are directed toward him as the only and **Main-Center of the Godhead**. In this way, the mind has a certain anchor and can recognize, understand, and comprehend the one whom it worships. Through this, we emerge from all doubt and do not need to wander back and forth in our thoughts seeking a being we wish to worship without knowing how he is, where he is, or who and what he is. Here we are delivered from the Antichrist, who has invented three persons of the Godhead and has made separate prayers to the Father, separate ones to the Son, and separate ones to the Holy Spirit. Must the mind not turn away from the One when it directs itself toward another specifically? Therefore, cast the idol-servants of the priests out of the house!

...you Jews, for of this your <term>Talmud</term> <note>The central text of Rabbinic Judaism, consisting of the Mishnah and the Gemara.</note> is only the image, which is called the oral law. It is not the oral law itself, but is just as much a written law as the two Testaments, which God wrote at the beginning of the world; and you understand the Talmud just as little as you do the <term>Old Testament</term>. How then could it explain the Old Testament to you as the written law? In the literal sense, all of these are merely images. The Old Testament followed the "Teaching of the Gods" <note>likely a reference to ancient pagan or polytheistic beliefs</note> and is called "the Law" to indicate that the preceding literal teachings of the heathens were not the true law. But in its literal form, the Old Testament was also not the true law, but only the image of it. After this followed the <term>New Testament</term> as the Gospel under the name of Christ, or the Messiah, to indicate that the Old Testament in its literal form was not the true law, but that the Messiah must first establish it. But in the literal form, it was not the Gospel, nor was it the Messiah. Therefore, the Talmud followed under the name of the "Second Law," through which the first law would be explained; but in the literal form, it was also not the second and oral law, for that was only to come at the very end of the Church. Therefore, the <term>Quran</term> <note>original: "Alcoran"</note> followed under the name of the last prophet, Muhammad; but in the literal form, it was not that either, but only the word of God of the last external major religions—and only now is the Messiah present as the last prophet.

Your Talmud is called the oral law for the reasons stated above. Now, when it is said that it was carried forward from Moses onward through oral narrations from generation to generation until it was first written down in a book after Christ, in the course of the New Testament era; this is again another figure and representation. In this regard, it depicts how the written Word of God in the external doctrine has been carried forward and preserved from the beginning of the world through oral teaching and preaching until the time of the Messiah, who explains it through writings and presents the true law of God through his mouth and pen. All of these are only images and riddles, and he who is wise, let him listen and improve himself: and he who is discerning, let him take counsel, that he may perceive the proverbs and their interpretation, the teaching of the wise and their riddles. ## The IX. Article.

§. 11. I believe with a perfect faith that this Law will never be changed: and that no other Law will be given by the Creator, whose name be blessed.

This current Law in the true teaching of the <term>Revealed Unity</term> <note>original: "Off. E.", likely standing for *Offenbarte Einheit* (Revealed Unity) or *Offenbarung Eliä* (Revelation of Elias), terms often used in radical pietist or mystical circles to describe their specific spiritual insights.</note> will never be changed, and God will never give another. A true Israelite must believe this with a perfect faith. You Jews cannot say this of your external Law of the <term>Old Testament</term>, for the <term>New Testament</term> followed it, as did the <term>Quran</term> <note>original: "Alcoran"</note> with other external laws. If, however, you wish to say that these two churches were not from God and that they possessed no Law of God, then you do not believe the First Article, according to which God made everything. He made the entire Church of all nations through His own Word, and there is no church on earth that is not grounded upon a Word of God. But when finally all nations are to become one—as the Old Testament testifies—then another Law, another teaching, must come, and all external teachings must cease, for it was precisely in those that they were divided. This other teaching is then the Law after which God will give no other.

## The X. Article.

§. 12. I believe with a perfect faith that the Creator, whose name be blessed, knows all the deeds of the children of men, as well as all their thoughts, according to the words of <term>Psalm 33:15</term>: "He who fashions their hearts altogether and considers all their works."

God knows and recognizes all external religious works, as well as the intentions of all religions, and knows that they are evil <note>In this context, "evil" likely refers to being spiritually hollow or "of the flesh" rather than purely malicious.</note>: therefore He gives the true Law to lead them from error to the truth. He also knows all the godless who, along with the <term>Antichrist</term>, will set themselves against it. He fashions a good heart when a person allows His Spirit space within themselves. But if a person is evil and suppresses their spirit, then the devil—who is also called "god" <note>A reference to the "god of this world" or the demiurge, a common theme in mystical and Gnostic-leaning Christian thought where the ego or the devil acts as a false deity.</note>—fashions the heart; yet God knows and sees it regardless. For because His Spirit is everywhere and is the eternal nature of God Himself, He knows how and where He finds an object <note>meaning a receptive soul or a point of connection</note> in a person, or not; and thus He knows the thoughts and intentions of all people.

### The XI. Article.

§. 13. I believe with a perfect faith that the Creator, blessed be His name, rewards with good those who keep His commandments, and punishes those who transgress His commandments.

Whoever keeps these commandments within this true law of the <term>Revelation of Christ</term> <note>original: "Off. C."; referring to an internal, spiritual revelation rather than mere outward observance.</note> will be rewarded by God with good, and whoever transgresses them will be punished. The reward shall be the world to come, as the Kingdom of the Messiah, just as this is interpreted; and the punishment shall be the destruction of the godless. The Messiah desires from God the preservation of upright people according to <term>Exodus 32:32</term> <note>original: "2. Mos. 32, 32"</note>. *Now forgive them their sin—in the external doctrine—and if not, blot me out of your book that you have written.* This is also added from the teachings of <term>Maimonides</term> <note>original: "Maimon"; refers to the 12th-century philosopher who formulated these 13 articles.</note>.

### The XII. Article.

§. 14. I believe with a perfect faith in the coming of the Messiah: and even though he may tarry, nonetheless I hope firmly in him at all times, until he comes.

The entire <term>Old Testament</term> <note>original: "A. T."</note> requires this faith, and according to such testimonies, it was impossible for the Jews to believe that the <term>priest-Messiah</term> <note>original: "Pfaffen-Meßias"; a derogatory term used here to describe the institutional Christian view of Jesus which the author argues did not fulfill the expected earthly prophecies.</note> of the Christians was the true Messiah, because under him that which should happen in the days of the Messiah did not occur.

### The XIII. Article.

§. 15. I believe with a perfect faith that the dead shall live again at the time when it pleases the Creator, blessed be His name, and may His memory be exalted for all eternity.

The resurrection of the dead is the resurrection from the death of the <term>literal doctrine</term> <note>original: "Buchstaben-Lehre"; literally "doctrine of the letter," implying a move from a superficial understanding of scripture to a spiritual one.</note> into the true doctrine; and the reappearance of the blessing in nature upon earth, arising out of the curse that has existed until now. The Messiah is the firstborn from the dead, and through him others must be made alive in the true doctrine; therefore, the resurrection of the dead is linked with the time of the Messiah. Along with this is also the <term>Final Judgment</term> <note>original: "Jüngste Gericht"</note>, where even the long-deceased godless ones, together with the godless who die in this judgment, shall be visibly placed before the court; and the Messiah must judge them from the Word of God, for which purpose the books of the Word of God are opened precisely in their true sense. <term>Daniel 7</term> <note>original: "Dan. 7"</note>.

->D 2<-

These, then, are the 13 Articles of Faith which, according to the explanation given thus far, are believed by true Israelites. <term>Maimonides</term> <note>original: "Maimon"; refers to the Sephardic philosopher Moses Maimonides.</note> says further: Whoever believes all of this perfectly belongs among the number of the true Israelites. Such a person is to be loved; one must have mercy upon him and show him all the good that God, as the Creator, commands that one should show to one's neighbor and brother out of true love and brotherly friendship. Let it be noted that God Himself spoke and wrote these words; consequently, He will also have mercy on all those and show them good who accept this teaching with heart-felt conviction. The religions are also brothers, and one is the neighbor of the other. Whoever, then, holds the faith of this doctrine also gladly shows good to all other religions, and thus all religions become one in this teaching. Further:

And even if such a person had committed all sins because of his <term>innate sinful nature</term> <note>original: "angebohrnen sündlichen Natur"; a reference to the concept of original sin or the "evil inclination" (yetzer hara).</note>, he will indeed be punished for his sin, but will nevertheless, along with other sinful Israelites, become a partaker of the future life—namely, of the **Kingdom of Christ**. The meaning here pertains primarily to the doctrine in which we have all erred and sinned. This is also punished in words as <term>idolatry</term> <note>original: "Abgötterey"</note>; but whoever accepts this doctrine as the truth and assents to it with heart and mouth will also be received into the Kingdom of Christ; or, if he dies beforehand, into eternal blessed life. A godless sinner who still repents of his wickedness and is converted is also not excluded from this, for God has sworn by Himself that *He does not desire the death of the sinner, but rather that he be converted and live,* **Ezekiel 21:32.** <note>The author cites Ezekiel 21:32, though the sentiment is more famously found in Ezekiel 18:23 and 33:11.</note> Further:

But whoever denies even a single one of these Articles of Faith, as they have now been explained, or presumes to belittle the same, does not belong to the Israelite Church. For he denies God and becomes a <term>heretic</term> <note>original: "Ketzer"</note> and an <term>Epicurean</term> <note>original: "Epicurer"; used here in the Jewish sense of "Apikoros," meaning a skeptic or one who denies divine revelation.</note>. He thereby uproots what was once planted and is worthy of being likewise uprooted and perishing. For the Scripture also says of such a one in **Psalm 139:21**: *I hate them, Lord, that hate thee*—namely, thee, our father Adam—*and I am grieved with those that rise up against thee.* <note>The author uniquely interprets "thee" in the Psalm as referring to "our father Adam," likely a reference to the mystical "Adam Kadmon" or the original state of humanity.</note> O thou pure and simple truth! Thou hast flowed from the mouth of God!

### How God applies Himself to the Law.

The Church is the day of 12 hours, because it is enclosed within the number 12 along with the Tribes and the Apostles. It is divided into 3 households and 4 principal religions. In the Pagan church, God taught the Law from His word written for that church. In the second church <note>The era of the Old Testament.</note>, He judged the external nature of the first church with the Old Testament, just as at the end in the Revelation of St. John the judgment proceeds from it. In the third church, He nourished them with the name of Jesus, in which all peoples were to find their salvation. This is also happening now at the end, and the Messiah comes out of the Christian church. But the right coupling is in the doctrine of the Revelation of Christ <note>original: "Off. C.", likely "Offenbarung Christi."</note>, which is the fourth after the three households.

# On God.

The formation of the outer Church in its six working days. The God who has made both the outer Church and the doctrine of all peoples, and who also creates the general Church through the true doctrine of His Word, that is the God of Israel.

Our <term>Baalspfaf</term> <note>literally "Baal-priest"; a derogatory term used by the author for an orthodox cleric he considers spiritually blind.</note> calls it vexing and blasphemous that the Rabbis would say God also "studies" the Law. But out of malice, this thief also translates the word <term>עסק</term> <term>asak</term> <note>original Hebrew: 'asak', meaning to occupy oneself, engage in, or be busy with.</note> as "studying," when it actually only means to occupy oneself with a matter or to be devoted to a thing. When a human being occupies himself with the Law of God, one can certainly call that "studying," because he is born in ignorance and must learn. But when this word is used regarding the actions of God, it must not be taken in that way, especially since its primary meaning is "to occupy oneself." God also teaches us through His Word and through His Spirit. But when the Rabbis say that God teaches the children, this priest accuses them of wanting to make a schoolmaster out of God; thus does this spider draw poison from all things.

## God teaches the children.

§. 6. The <term>Yalkut Shimoni</term> <note>A significant medieval midrashic collection.</note> on Isaiah, folio 50, column 4, number 316, says:
> "What does He do in the fourth part of the day? He sits and teaches the school children the
> Law, according to Isaiah 28:9, where it says: 'To whom shall he teach knowledge? Or
> whom shall he make to understand what is heard? To whom does he teach knowledge?
> To those who are weaned from the milk and taken from the breasts.'"

Here, the three households <note>referring to historical-spiritual dispensations</note> in the outer doctrine are taken as the three parts of the day, and the doctrine of the <term>Off. C.</term> <note>likely an abbreviation for *Offenbarung Christi* (Revelation of Christ).</note> is the fourth part. Here, God teaches knowledge to those who are taken away from the "milk" and the "breasts" of the outer doctrine. David prays: *Lord, show me your ways, and teach me your paths*, and all believers are taught by God: thus there is nothing offensive in this at all. But God only teaches the humble children, and no proud priest who is so blind that he believes he knows everything, yet knows nothing at all.

# On God.

...nothing other than a hint of the inner and outer meaning of the Word of God, "for the outer law has the shadow of future things, and not the essence of the goods themselves: and the outer church and doctrine is the Tabernacle of Moses, which was only a prototype of the heavenly things in the Kingdom of the Messiah"—Hebrews chapters 9 and 10. Now, for the first time, the doors are opening to the inner spiritual sense of the Word of God. But when we ourselves enter into this Kingdom of God on earth, we shall first see the wonders that lie hidden within God's Word.

Regarding the great <term>Rabbi Isaac Luria</term> <note>A 16th-century mystic and founder of Lurianic Kabbalah, often called the "Ari."</note>, the book *Emek Hammelech* <note>original: "Emek hammelech", meaning "The Valley of the King," a major Kabbalistic work by Naftali Hertz ben Yaakov Elchanan.</note> reports in the section titled "The Author's Introduction," chapter 2, folio 10, column 2: 
> "He was so worthy that his soul ascended every night to the High School <note>A reference to the "Yeshivah shel Ma'alah" or the Heavenly Academy.</note>; then the hosts of ministering angels came to protect him on the way until they had brought him into the School of the Greatest. There they would ask him: In which school did he desire to sit? Whereupon he would sometimes choose the school of <term>Rabbi Simeon ben Jochai</term> <note>The traditional author of the Zohar.</note>, sometimes the school of <term>Rabbi Akiva</term>, sometimes the school of <term>Rabbi Eliezer the Great</term>, and sometimes the school of the Prophets."

This is an image of how we are led out of the night of outer doctrine into the Upper School of true doctrine, which is the right school of the Prophets. The three preceding schools indicate the Word of God in the "Three Dispensations" <note>A theological concept referring to different eras of God's dealings with humanity—usually the ages of Nature, the Law, and Grace.</note>, wherein we shall wander at our pleasure, now in this one, now in that: sometimes looking back at the past things of the outer Church, and sometimes looking forward at the eternal things.

The <term>Midrash Koheleth</term> <note>A rabbinic commentary on the Book of Ecclesiastes.</note>, folio 323, column 2, says: 
> "Rabbi Jochanan speaks: Everyone who exerts himself in the Law in this world, they do not let him sleep in the future world, but lead him into the school of <term>Shem</term> and <term>Eber</term> <note>Biblical ancestors traditionally associated with the preservation of divine wisdom before Abraham.</note>, and of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, and of Moses and Aaron." 

These are seven schools, which represent the true doctrine in all the Word of God, into which we shall be led in the future world, namely in the Kingdom of the Messiah. But only those are led into them who have occupied themselves with the Word of God here in this time and have built themselves up within it. From this, one can also infer how few will enter this kingdom, and how true the words of Christ are: **Many are called, but few are chosen.** This is also quite natural, for what should such "deadened" people do in this kingdom, who never had a delight in the Word of God or a hunger for it? Furthermore, these words testify that there will be no more sleeping in this kingdom, but rather a ceaseless occupation with the Word of God.

## Two Higher Schools.

§. 7. *Yalkut Hadash* <note>original: "Jalkut chadasch", a 17th-century collection of Kabbalistic midrashim.</note>, folio 115, column 4, under the title *Malachim* <note>original: "Malachim", meaning "Angels".</note>, number 24, says from the *Zohar*:
> "There are 2 upper schools, one above the other. One is the
> "School of the Firmament <note>original: "Veste", referring to the biblical 'rakia' or expanse of heaven.</note>, and the other is above it. In the highest school,
> "no objections or contrary questions arise: But in the School of the Firmament,
> "they exist. All objections raised therein are resolved in the highest
> "school. In the future, however, there will be no more objections even in the School of the Firmament,
> "for to this the words point in Psalm 72:7 <note>The text quotes "Peace be within your walls," which is actually found in Psalm 122:7.</note>:
> "May there be peace within your walls, and rest within your palaces."

Just as the doctrine of the outer church is also called a "heaven," it is also called a high or upper school. In this outer doctrine are the contentious questions, which are resolved in the highest school of true doctrine; then they shall be no more, but all peoples will live in unity and peace. God's Word teaches with parables and always sets two things against each other, so that one must conclude the one from the other, and recognize each thing by its opposite. If one applies these two upper schools to the teaching of the <term>Revelation</term> <note>original: "Off. C.", likely "Offenbarung Christi," referring to the Book of Revelation.</note>; then the School of the Firmament is the teaching of <term>Revelation</term> as it is in this current time, where it deals only with contrary objections and must tear down "Babylon" <note>A symbolic reference to the corrupted or confused outer church.</note>. In that case, in the future school, this struggle of Michael against the Dragon is no longer necessary; instead, there is peace and rest, and the spirit occupies itself in tranquility and joy with the wonders of God in His Word. The firmament of clouds also encompasses the lower things on earth; therefore, the teaching of <term>Revelation</term> in this current time must still occupy itself with many outer things. But when it passes from this School of the Firmament into the highest school, it is in the "waters" or teachings above the firmament, and has the mysteries of the starry heaven as its subject.

§. 8. *Yalkut Hadash*, folio 170, column 2, number 43, from the book *Tikkune Zohar Hadash* <note>A collection of appendices to the Zohar focusing on the first word of the Torah.</note>, under the title *Torah*, says:
> "To the <term>House of Hillel</term> and the <term>House of Shammai</term> <note>Two famous opposing schools of Jewish thought in the 1st century.</note>
> "are opposed two teachers of the <term>Gemara</term> <note>The component of the Talmud comprising rabbinical analysis and commentary.</note> in the firmament, namely Michael and
> "Gabriel: but Uriel gives the verdict between them."

The two houses are the two Testaments <note>The Old and New Testaments of the Bible.</note>, and Michael and Gabriel are the same. In the literal sense, the two Testaments are set against one another. But Uriel, which means "Light of God," is the teaching of the <term>Revelation</term>, which gives the verdict between both. See Rabbi Menachem of Recanati <note>A 13th-14th century Italian Kabbalist.</note> on the Five Books of Moses, folio 97, column 2, <term>Parashah Yitro</term> <note>The weekly Torah portion containing the Ten Commandments.</note>. Also, *Yalkut Reubeni* the Great <note>original: "Jalkut rubeni gadol", a collection of Kabbalistic commentaries by Reuben Hoeshke.</note>, folio 159, column 3, <term>Parashah Phinehas</term>.

# How Souls Learn from Books After Death.

The small book *Forgotten Gleanings* <note>original: "Schechechat leket"</note>, under the title *Acts of Loving-kindness and Charity* <note>original: "gemiluth chasadim uzedaka"</note>, number 4, taken from the book *Secrets of Secrets* <note>original: "Sode rase"</note>, discusses this. And the *Book of the Pious* <note>original: "Sepher chasadim"</note>, number 455, says: "The souls have books lying ready on the table. <margin>*</margin> And just as they were accustomed to learning in their lives, so they also learn in their death." This death is the passing away of the external doctrine <note>The "external doctrine" refers to a literal or superficial understanding of religion.</note>, and the resurrection into the true doctrine. Whoever enjoyed reading God's Word in the external doctrine and was edified by it will then find the books of God's Word lying ready in the Kingdom of Christ and learn from them. These words indicate how God's Word will still benefit deceased people even after their death—specifically those who are on the path to their redemption; for everything the ear has ever heard of God's Word can indeed be presented to the memory of the mind. In the Kingdom of Christ, however, there is still a special interaction through God's Word with those souls who are yet to be redeemed.

In the aforementioned book, number 456, one reads: "It happened that strangers passed by a burial place and saw a Jew who had his book on the table and was reading from it." The burial place is the time when the external doctrine is buried. Then the strangers, who do not belong to the Israel of God, will see that the true Jews or confessors will nevertheless read from God's Word. This is a miracle: that the entire external doctrine of God's Word and literal history falls away, and yet a much more powerful doctrine remains within it, which is the resurrection of a new doctrine from the death and dust of the literal teaching <note>original: "Buchstabenlehre", meaning a rigid, rule-bound interpretation of scripture.</note>. This fits his mockery quite well. Let us hear the words of the Talmud!

Then he comes down to earth again and studies in the school of the earth."

### How God Wept for Four Reasons.

<margin>The Talmud, Tractate Chagigah, folio 5, column 2, concerning the words of Jeremiah 13:17, says this about it:</margin>
§ 9. The Rabbis teach that God wept for four reasons. First, because of the destruction of the Temple...

> “The Holy God has a place where He weeps, which is called *Mistarin* <note>meaning ‘a hidden place’ or ‘secret chambers’</note>. But what do the words <term>מפני גוה</term> <gloss>mipne gevah</gloss> mean? (That is: because of pride, over which God secretly weeps, Jeremiah 13:17.) For Rav Papa says: With God there is no sadness, as it is said in 1 Chronicles 16:27: ‘Glory and splendor are before His face, strength and joy are in His place.’ Answer: This objection is nothing, for this is meant for the houses of the dwellings—the outer houses. Is it not so? Behold, it is written in Isaiah 22:12: ‘Therefore the Lord Sabaoth <note>original: "Zebaoth"; a Hebrew title for God meaning "Lord of Hosts"</note> will cause a call to go forth at that time for weeping and mourning, and for baldness and the putting on of sackcloth.’ It is a different matter here with the destruction of the Temple, for even the angels of peace wept over it, as it is written in Isaiah 33:7: ‘Behold, their mighty ones cry out without, and the angels of peace weep bitterly.’”

The weeping of God must be understood as occurring in nature and the creature on earth, for the Spirit of God creates sorrow and weeping in the believers over the ungodliness through which righteousness and truth are suppressed. In the external church, the sanctuary of the Word of God was handed over to the children of the world, and the inner part was destroyed and suppressed.

### How Souls Learn from Books After Death.

This is discussed in the little book *Forgotten Gleanings* <note>original: "Schechechat leket"</note>, under the title *The Bestowing of Kindness and Righteousness* <note>original: "gemiluth chasadim uzedaka"</note> no. 4, from the book *The Secret of Mysteries* <note>original: "Sode-raze"</note>. And the *Book of the Pious* <note>original: "Sepher chasidim"</note>, no. 455, says: “The souls have books lying ready on the table. And just as they were accustomed to learning in their life, so they also learn in their death.” This death is the dying away of the external teaching, and the rising again in the true teaching. Whoever enjoyed reading God’s Word in the external teaching and was edified by it will then also find the books of the Word of God lying ready in the Kingdom of Christ and learn from them. These sayings also indicate how the Word of God will still be of use to deceased persons even after their death—namely, to those who are on the way to their redemption; for everything the ear has ever heard of the Word of God can very well be presented to the memory of the mind. In the Kingdom of Christ, however, there is still a special interaction through the Word of God with those souls who are yet to be redeemed.

In the previously cited book, no. 456, one reads: “It happened that strangers passed by a place of burial and saw a Jew who had his book on the table and was reading from it.” The place of burial is the time when the external teaching is buried. There, the strangers who do not belong to the Israel of God will see that the true Jews or confessors will nevertheless read in God's Word. This is a wonder: namely, that the entire external teaching of the Word of God and the literal history falls away, and yet a much more powerful teaching remains within it, which is the resurrection of a new teaching from the death and dust of the literal teaching. Our priest of Baal <note>a derogatory term for a corrupt or worldly clergyman, likening him to the idolatrous priests of the Old Testament</note> spits his bile over all of this and says here: "If only the fable were true!" # On God.

The book *Pesiqta Rabbati* <note>original: "Pfikta rabbetha," a collection of medieval Jewish homilies</note>, folio 52, columns 2 and 3, says: Since the destruction of the Temple, God no longer sits upon His throne. Likewise, the destruction of the Temple and the current misery of the Jews is said to be the cause of earthquakes. Likewise, *Me'or Einayim* <note>A 16th-century work of Jewish history and criticism</note>, folio 6, column 1.

All of this must be sought within nature on earth and in the external church. Hitherto, the inner temple was destroyed, and the holy God did not hold dominion on earth; instead, the god of this world—the devil—held it, though he still had his limits. Therefore, God did not sit upon His throne in the outer nature on earth or in the church: and for this reason Christ says: *My kingdom is not of this world.* When the worldly governments break apart, only then does the kingdom of the Most High come upon the earth, and then He sits upon His throne again (Daniel 7). The kingdom of Christ is also called the Heavenly Jerusalem, to be considered in contrast to the lower Jerusalem of the external Christian church. Thus, He also does not enter this Heavenly Jerusalem until the Israel of the believers also enters therein. The time for this is firmly determined, and that is the oath which God has taken in this regard. However, the Heavenly Jerusalem of God indicates something more here, namely the transformation of the planetary heavens, where the planets must stand still again, and God will also rest therein from His previous works.

The 4 ells, which God is said to have walked after the destruction of the Temple, are the 4 main religions of the church, within which He has walked with His Word, and no further, for there have become no more than 4 main religions. The destruction of God’s inner temple was also the cause of earthquakes and all manner of destruction in nature. It was the cause of the misery of the Jews and of all people. Therefore, when this temple of blessing is restored in nature, all misery, lamentation, and distress on earth will come to an end. Our priest of Baal <note>original: "Baalspfaff," a derogatory term for a false or corrupt clergyman whom the author likely views as an opponent</note> mocks and blasphemes all these things. But that was already his own punishment; for because he was a godless thief, God locked him out of the paradise-garden of wisdom, so that he could not see, taste, or enjoy the lovely fruit in these things. Instead, he had to eat poison and gall from them, which permeated his marrow and soul, and brought him to the poisonous place of hell, where he belongs as if in his own element.

### How God may be Forced to Do Something.

§. 13. The Rabbis have various expressions regarding how God can be compelled to do something or to refrain from doing it. The **Talmud** <note>The central collection of Jewish law and tradition.</note> Tractate **Taanit** <note>The volume concerning fast days and prayers for rain.</note>, folio 19, column 1, recounts how **Chonai** <note>Known as Honi ha-M'agel or "Honi the Circle-Maker," a Jewish scholar of the 1st century BC famous for his miracle-working prayer for rain.</note> drew a circle and forced God to make it rain. Tractate **Bava Metzia** <note>The volume dealing with civil law and property.</note>, folio 28, column 2, likewise confirms such things, as does Tractate **Taanit**, folio 23, column 1, where it is stated: Chonai, through an incantation <note>original: *Beschwörung*</note>, caused drops of water to fall as large as a hole measuring six eggshells in size.

All of this is correct, provided it is properly understood. Regarding **Job**, God also says to **Satan**: "You have incited <note>or "persuaded" or "seduced"</note> me to ruin him without cause" (Job 2:3). And it is written of **Christ** that they bound him and dragged him back and forth. In the time leading up to now, the holy God has relinquished His dominion on earth (Luke 4:6) and abandoned it to the god of this world <note>A reference to the devil, following the language of 2 Corinthians 4:4.</note>. Consequently, His holy power was bound upon the earth and possessed the least amount of influence—though it never worked in league with evil, and it did place restraints upon the darkness. He was the master of the house of whom Christ spoke in the parable, saying that He had gone away to a far country and handed over the governance of the house to His servants, whom He would, however, call to account upon His return. Because the curse and evil held the upper hand on earth, and because this was confined within a set limit of how long it should last, God could not help the poor and the miserable, even though it was His will that they should be helped. The unmerciful judges and rulers were able to "force" and restrain Him so that no help occurred. Similarly, He willed that the believers should live without sin, and they indeed exerted themselves toward that end; yet it could not be, because the devil held supremacy and continually worked evil and corruption within them. # God has from the beginning created Satan and Evil.

§. 15. The rabbis further teach: That God created the evil nature of man and the evil spirits. Both are understood under the <term>Yetzer hara</term> <note>original: יצר הרע; literally "the evil inclination." In Jewish thought, this is the innate impulse toward self-interest or sin, which must be mastered rather than destroyed.</note>. <term>Yetzer</term> means the will, desire, or inclination, and <term>ra</term> means evil; thus <term>Yetzer hara</term> means the evil will, the evil manner, inclination, and desire. And because such things come from Satan and his evil spirits, the satanic nature itself is also understood by this term, along with all evil spirits. God himself made and created all of this at the beginning of the world through his own arrangement, because the satanic nature was necessary for the work of creation during the time leading up to the present. From the effect of this satanic nature, the evil manner and inclination in man further arose, and no human on earth was entirely free from it. But whoever has particularly surrendered themselves to the satanic nature—in pride, enmity, discord, malice, deceit, violence, unmercifulness, and the like—he was also Satan’s servant in a very special way. But that God himself made Satan, and consequently evil, He himself testifies when He speaks in Isaiah 45:7: "I who make the light, and create the darkness: I who make peace, and create evil. I, Jehovah, do all these things." God therefore made Satan, but what Satan further effects, the holy God does not effect: and what the ungodly do under the influence and impulse of Satan, the holy God does not do.

The Talmud, Tractate Berakhot, folio 61, column 1 says: "And the Lord God <term>yatzar</term> <note>original: יצר; 'formed'</note>, formed Adam," as is read in Genesis 2:7: where the word <term>vayiytzer</term> <note>original: וייצר</note>, namely "he formed," is written with two *Yods* <note>The Hebrew letter 'Y'. The author is pointing out a traditional scribal curiosity where the word is spelled with two 'y's instead of one.</note>, namely יי. This indicates that God created two types or natures: one, the good nature, or <term>Yetzer tov</term> <note>The "good inclination" or impulse toward divine will.</note>, and one the evil nature, or <term>Yetzer ra</term>. See <note>original: *Vid.*; Latin *vide*, meaning 'see'.</note> also the book *Shefa Tal* <note>A 17th-century Kabbalistic text by Shabbethai Sheftel Horowitz that discusses the emanation of divine light.</note>, folio 91, column 3; and the *Yalkut Shimoni* <note>A massive medieval compilation of Midrashic interpretations of the Hebrew Bible.</note> on Job, folio 149, column 2, no. 906.

There is no human on earth who does not have evil and corruption in them, but yet with a very great difference. They are lowly and despised, while the godless walk tall and rule. The regents are generally godless people who care the least about God, yet they rule over others. They live in luxury and glory, and squander the bitter sweat of the poor, who meanwhile often do not have enough bread to be full. That is the greatest injustice, and the poor Jewish people testify to this in a tangible image. They are also God’s children, just as much as other people, and yet God lets them go like dogs, and has given them neither land nor sand. <note>The phrase "neither land nor sand" is an old German idiom meaning to possess absolutely nothing.</note> They are despised and a mockery of the people, and in this they carry the image of the inner church of believers among all nations. All of this is injustice itself, and therein God judges unjustly. 

But in this matter, one must keep one's eye fixed only on the world as it has been until now, and not on the connection of this time with the future: for when one considers things in their connection, then everything is good, and this time had to be so for the sake of the future time. God reveals to us through these things what this time, and the external church and teaching are—namely, pure injustice, in which the true teaching and also the true God were not present, according to 2 Chronicles 15:3. <note>2 Chronicles 15:3: "For a long time Israel was without the true God, without a priest to teach and without the law."</note> Consequently, we should look around for the true teaching and the true God. This God, however, is our father Adam, who allowed the current curse to come upon us himself, but now wishes to take it away again and place us in the land of blessing, for which he created us. <note>This is a highly unusual mystical claim, suggesting that the "True God" to be revealed is the restored, primordial humanity (Adam), who acts as a redemptive figure.</note>

The righteous shall be named after you: Jacob the Small, Samuel the Small, David the Small. That is to say, when David, Jacob, and Samuel stand in the image of the *outer Christ* <note>The "outer Christ" refers to the physical or literal manifestation of divinity in history, as opposed to the internal spiritual reality.</note>, they are called "Small," and the righteous shall be named after the name of Jesus. But the New Testament, in its true sense, is not satisfied with all of this, and it desires no such "outer" Christ. This Christ, God has made into sin, and has thereby sinned; for that reason, he is killed and rooted out along with the sin, and in this process, a Sacrifice of Atonement occurs, in which God and humanity are reconciled. Therefore God says—because the moon would not be satisfied—"Bring a Sacrifice of Atonement because I have made the moon lesser." <note>This refers to a famous Jewish Midrash where the moon complains that two kings (sun and moon) cannot wear the same crown, leading God to diminish the moon’s light.</note> This Sacrifice of Atonement is now the true doctrine, which the moon, as the New Testament, desires to have: and this is what Resh Lakish <note>A prominent 3rd-century Jewish scholar/Amora.</note> says: "Oh, how entirely different is the goat that is sacrificed at the New Moon, in the new doctrine of the Revelation of Christ!" This is a completely different doctrine than the external doctrine of the literal word! This new doctrine is the sin offering to the Lord (Numbers 28:15). Through this doctrine, God is justified, and so is man: for God had to create the evil—the *Jezer hara* <note>original: "Jezer hara"; the Hebrew term for the "evil inclination" or the innate impulse toward self-interest/evil.</note>—out of necessity, so that we humans could be created for eternal glory; therefore, it is not reckoned to Him as sin. We, however, out of a necessary consequence of the condition of nature—which God Himself made thus—have been unable to live without sin; therefore, it is also not reckoned to us.

Rabbi Bechai <note>Bahya ben Asher, a 13th-century Spanish rabbi and kabbalist.</note>, in his commentary on folio 134, column 1, says: the word <term>כפרה (Kapparah) <gloss>Atonement</gloss></term> is used for nothing other than sin. Because, therefore, the aforementioned sin offering was to be "to the Lord," He has also sinned, as He Himself says. But for all that, the holy God does not sin, for the inner remains distinct from the outer, and He only reckons the sin to Himself because He placed the "outer" in such a condition, and even entered into the corruption of nature with His own body at the beginning of the world. See, this is how it is that Christ has taken our sin upon Himself.

This is a beautiful illustration of how God, out of necessity, had to speak differently in the letter than what He actually meant. He spoke in the way that the **external man** liked to hear, and it had to be so; for otherwise, Sarah, as the Christian Church, would not have loved Abraham, or Jesus Christ, since the name of Jesus was intended to be made known externally.

The words of the wise are thus like spears and nails, planted—or spread out in the external doctrine—by the masters of assemblies (meaning the religions), but given by a single Shepherd, who is Jesus Christ our **father Adam**, <note>Reference to Ecclesiastes 12:11, which discusses the "words of the wise."</note>. The learned foxes, who grasp these spears and nails in their foolhardy and daring way, pierce their own hands with them: for these words are like bacon on a fox-trap, meant for them to bite and be caught. Our <term>Baal-priest<note>original: *Baals-Pfaf*; a derogatory term used by radical dissenters to label established church clergy as false prophets or idolaters.</note></term> has bitten hard here and says: "This matter is not to be found in the history of Abraham; these are doctrines hatched by the devil, and Satan, as the falsifier of Holy Scripture, gave these blasphemous things to the **Rabbis** to contemplate." See how he can lie! He himself is indeed Satan, and God wrote these things. But since he has not attributed them to God, he is the Satan, who has been a liar from the beginning of his priestly office, and in whom the truth has never resided. In the New Testament, things from the Old Testament are very often cited differently than they actually appear in the Old Testament; but for that reason, the New Testament is not a doctrine of the devil, and the same applies to the <term>Talmud<note>The central text of Rabbinic Judaism. For God's word has a manifold sense, which God allows us to recognize precisely by interpreting a matter one way and then another through the Rabbis.

### How God has defiled Himself.

§. 22. ## How God Prays.

§. 25. When it is said that God prays, this naturally refers to His Spirit within the believers on earth, or in His Word, wherein He teaches us to pray and has prescribed for us the manner of prayer. <term>Bodenschatz<note>Johann Christoph Georg Bodenschatz (1717–1797), a German theologian who wrote extensively on Jewish customs, though often from a critical or polemical perspective.</note></term>—whom I shall henceforth call nothing other than <term>Sammael<note>The name of an archangel in Talmudic and post-Talmudic lore, often associated with the Accuser, the Angel of Death, or a figure of severity and malice; the author uses it here as a derogatory nickname for Bodenschatz.</note></term>—has collected all these things out of venom and gall against the Jews, in order to display them to their shame and as a spectacle, and has particularly fragmented this article. Since I do not have the books myself, I cannot know with what intention this or that is said in the <term>Talmud<note>The central text of Rabbinic Judaism, consisting of the Mishnah and the Gemara.</note></term> or by the Rabbis; however, I will set down what he cites. The prayer of God from the Talmud is said to be this:

> May it be my pleasure <note>Original: *Wohlgefallen*; in this context, "May it be my Will."</note> that my mercy overcomes my wrath, and that my mercy envelops all my attributes, so that I may deal with my children according to the attribute of my mercy, and not execute my judgment upon them according to strictness. This is said to be based on Isaiah 56:7, where it says: "I will make them joyful in my house of prayer." Because it says "in my [house]," and not "in theirs," it follows that God must have a special house of prayer in which He prays. *Yalkut Chadash*, folio 5, column 3, number 32; *Yalkut Shimoni* on the Psalms, number 873, folio 113, column 3, titled <term>Churban<note>Original: *Chorban*; Hebrew for "Destruction," usually referring to the destruction of the Temple in Jerusalem.</note></term>.

Man is the temple of God in which He dwells, and in the time to come in the Kingdom of Christ, there will be a special tabernacle of God among men, and He will dwell among them as in a tabernacle, and they [will]...

## God does nothing without consulting with the angels.
### That is, God does nothing on earth without means <note>The author is interpreting "angels" as the natural or spiritual "means" through which God acts, rather than independent beings making decisions for Him.</note>.

The meaning of this, however, is this: that the blessed Creator makes all His works through means or mediators. We also find in the literal sense of the Law proofs which confirm this, and for this reason God speaks here in the plural <note>original: "Plurali"</note> or in the multiple: "Let us make men," or "make Adam," in order thereby to indicate the means.

The holy angels and the inner, true teachings of the Word of God are understood under the same name, just as here the watchers and the speech of the holy ones stand together. In the inner true sense of the Word of God lies described the purpose and counsel of how everything shall go, and where everything shall ultimately come to an end. Because God now does everything on earth in the Church through His Word, as through a means; so also the true teachings in the Revelation of John are the angels or the upper family through which He makes the universal Church, and the actual holy angels also assist in this. For a single universal Church, there must also be a single universal doctrine, and the teachers who teach this doctrine are then also called angels, who help to create the new Church-Adam and the new Church-world. Just so were the external teachings and external teachers also angels, who helped to form the Adam of the external Church. Therefore God says in the plural: "Let us make Adam." # How God blows into a horn three times.

§. 29. God is said to blow the trumpet three times. The first time for the resurrection of the dead. The second time to uproot the seed of Amalek or Esau—which are one and the same, and by which the Rabbis understand the Christian Church <note>In the context of this manuscript's radical theology, "Amalek" and "Esau" represent the institutional or "corrupt" church that relies on outward power rather than inward spirit</note>. (Latin: vide)</note> *Machsor* <term>Machsor: A Jewish prayer book used for festivals</term>, folio 60, column 2.

These are the three outcomes of the Revelation of Christ, which all three have the same purpose. The resurrection of the dead is the resurrection from the death of the external "letter-teaching" <note>The literal, uninspired interpretation of scripture</note>. The uprooting of Amalek is the uprooting of all clerical teachings, along with all spiritual and worldly regimes: and the gathering of the Israelites is the gathering of all the godly from all nations into the teaching of the Revelation of Christ. The Scripture says itself, in Zechariah 9:14: "And the Lord <note>original: "Adonai"</note> Jehovah will blow the trumpet." Likewise: "God goes up with loud trumpets," Psalm 47:5 <note>The source cites Ps 47:6 following different verse numbering</note>. "He will send His angels with a loud trumpet," Matthew 24:31. "The trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised," 1 Corinthians 15:52. Here we see how the blowing is attributed to God Himself, and yet also to the angels; so it is also with teaching, praying, sinning, captivity, and all things previously mentioned, which the Talmud says of God. From such teachings we learn to seek God near us, within ourselves and by ourselves; this does not please Samael <term>Samael: In this context, an adversarial figure or "the accuser" who represents the forces that want to keep man separate from God</term>, as he places God far away in a heaven, of which heaven he cannot even say where it is; and thus he alone wishes to be lord on earth. But his kingdom has an end, and the accuser is cast down.

For the Old Testament teaches a single God. C."; likely referring to the Revelation of Jesus Christ (the Apocalypse) or a specific mystical commentary.</note> is called the Holy Spirit, and to this belongs again the first name, Jehovah, for the doctrine of the Revelation of C. is primarily drawn from the Old Testament.

The two Testaments were distinguished from one another in the letter <note>That is, in their literal, outward reading.</note>. If, however, they are brought into one sense, then this doctrine is the 3rd—namely the Spirit and true sense of the Word of God, which proceeds from the Father and Son, or from the Old and New Testaments, and these three are one. What the New Testament teaches of God and Jesus Christ is, in its true spiritual sense, exactly what the Old Testament teaches of them. The words Fire, Air, and Water are, as 3, only the numerical sign and parable; and just as these 3 are distinct, so too come different doctrines—the external and internal doctrine—from the Word of God. Therefore it is said: See, a mystery is hidden in a word that one hears, namely in the Word of God that one hears, and which yet is only one word.

The Sammael <note>The author's derogatory nickname for his Jewish opponent.</note> says: It is very remarkable that the Zohar <note>The foundational work of Jewish Kabbalah.</note> says in this passage: One recognizes the Trinity from the revelation of the Holy Spirit; since no one can be certainly convinced of such divine matters who is not particularly enlightened by the Holy Spirit.

But if this mystery were nothing other than the Priest-Trinity <note>original: "Pfaffen-Dreyeinigkeit"; a derogatory term for mainstream church dogma.</note> of the Christians; then all the thieves and murderers among the Christians would also have to be particularly enlightened by the Holy Spirit, for they all believe that there are supposed to be 3 Persons of the Godhead. Sammael, who is like them, therefore also imagines himself to be particularly enlightened by the Holy Spirit, and the Jews not at all. But he almost grants something of the Holy Spirit to the Zohar, a book which God himself has written. However, he thinks that the Zohar—that is, God—was not nearly as enlightened by the Holy Spirit as he is; therefore he still "improves" it where God has done it too poorly.

§. 2. In this very same book of the Zohar <note>original: "Sohar"; a foundational work of Jewish mysticism (Kabbalah).</note>, folio 31, column 2, the following is written:

The teachings are also called "gods" because they have ruled and governed in the Church, and God has governed through them. However, through the true doctrine, only the true eternal God, the Holy Spirit, works. The "highest God" mentioned here is thus the doctrine of the Old Testament, and the "God of the Fear of Isaac" is the New Testament, in which Isaac was sacrificed—or rather, the true Jesus Christ was crucified. For the Old Testament, which is actually the "Isaac" of the New Testament, was suppressed, and the Old Testament Church experienced its great terror; therefore, He is called the God of the Fear, or the Terror, of Isaac. C."; likely *Offenbarung Christi*, referring to the final revelation or the Apocalypse.</note>, which comes out of the Old Testament; and so Christ is the First and the Last. The Christians thus had the Old Testament, which is the Father; and they had the New Testament, which is the Son; and the New Testament also speaks much of the Holy Spirit, which, however, only looks toward the doctrine of the Revelation of C. at the end. But they took all of this according to the letter <note>That is, a literal rather than spiritual interpretation.</note> and took this three-fold nature of the doctrine as 3 persons of the Godhead, not understanding that the teachings themselves are called by the name "God." Thus, God drew near to them in the name of Jesus in the plurality. But these were only many powers in the doctrine of the Word of God—inner and outer teachings—which nevertheless came from the single Word of God, and which in their true sense are only one, and teach a single God.

Here, the Word of God is considered only in two aspects. By "the Word," the outward teaching is meant, and by "the Spirit," the true teaching in the <unclear>H. C.</unclear> <note>Likely an abbreviation for *Heiligen Christenthum* (Holy Christianity) or *Heiligen Communis* (Holy Community/Church).</note> The inner teaching lay hidden within the outer, and the Spirit also worked upon the believers through the same, according to the measure of each era. The sound of a word is also the first thing that presents itself externally to the ear, and the spirit, sense, or understanding of the word is indeed within the sounding word, yet it only makes itself comprehensible as a second and following thing. Sammael <note>In Jewish tradition, Sammael is an accuser or fallen angel; here, the author likely uses the name as a derogatory pseudonym for a theological opponent who argues for the personhood of the Trinity.</note> believes he has found proof here that even the ancient Jews considered the Holy Spirit to be a distinct person of the Godhead, but he has missed the mark widely.

They held as God not only the Holy Spirit, but also Jehovah <note>the personal name of God</note>, Elohim <note>God as Creator/Judge</note>, El <note>the Mighty One</note>, Shaddai <note>the Almighty</note>, Jah <note>a shortened form of the divine name</note>, Mekom <note>original: "Mekom"; the Place</note>, Shamayim <note>original: "Schamajim"; the Heavens</note>, and the Shekhinah <note>original: "Schechina"; the Divine Presence</note>; but they did not, for that reason, make as many "persons" out of them as Sammael has done.

The *Yalkut Reubeni* <note>original: "Jalkut rubeni"; a 17th-century collection of Kabbalistic midrashim.</note> no. 1, title *Beria* <note>Creation</note>, from the Midrash of Rabbi Nehunyah <note>original: "Nechunja"; likely referring to Nehunyah ben Ha-Kanah, a 1st-century sage.</note> says: 
> "Through the pure Word of God were the heaven and the earth created, and through his Holy Spirit were created all the upper hosts." 

This is one and the same as the previous point and refers to the outer and inner teaching.

> "After they had gone out of the sea, He let them go in the wilderness like cattle that gradually go down into a valley. Thus did the Spirit of God lead the Israelites." 

This is intended to be a proof for Sammael that Ben Ezra also considered the Holy Spirit to be a person of the Godhead. But let us see what the meaning of these words is.

Our scoffer <note>The author's opponent in this theological debate.</note> wants to prove herewith that the ancient **Jews** regarded the Holy Spirit as the **Lord** of the world, and as **Jehovah**, who can raise the dead. The Holy Spirit was certainly present here with **Ezekiel**, namely, the true teaching lay hidden within the outward teaching; but in the "letter" they were nothing but dead bones <note>A reference to Ezekiel 37 and the Vision of the Valley of Dry Bones.</note>, and with these dead bones they wanted to prove that the Holy Spirit is a distinct person of the Godhead. Is that not marvelous, since they believe nothing of the Holy Spirit—that is, the true teaching—and do not believe that God can make these dead bones live again?

He now proceeds to the newer **Rabbis**, who are, however, just as old as the former ones. "These newer ones are said to be very erroneous, even truly blasphemous in the doctrine of the Holy Spirit, because they understand it only as a certain kind of prophecy." Let us hear them!

§ 6. **Rabbi Menahem of Recanati** <note>original: *R. Menachem von Rekanat*; a 13th-century Italian Kabbalist and commentator.</note> regarding the 5th Book of Moses <note>Deuteronomy.</note> folio 83, column 3, Portion *Va'era* <note>original: *Parascha Vaêra*; though *Va'era* is usually in Exodus, the author is citing Recanati's specific commentary structure.</note> says:

> “Know that **prophecy** is drawn from the Crown <note>In Kabbalah, the *Kether* or Crown is the highest of the divine emanations.</note>, and is divided into 3 parts. The first part is called **prophecy**, and this the prophets attained, upon whom be peace. The second part is called the Holy Spirit, and this was attained by David, Solomon, and Daniel, and the other saints, and this part is lesser than **prophecy**. The third part is called **Bath Kol**,” (the Daughter of the Voice) <note>original: *Bath Kol*; an audible divine voice that provided guidance after the era of biblical prophecy had ended.</note> “and this part is lesser than the Holy Spirit, or is beneath the Holy Spirit: and this the Sages of Israel attained after the spirit of prophecy had ceased: and no one heard this **Bath Kol** except those who were crowned with wisdom and piety, through which they also saw hidden things, according to the words of Daniel 10:7: ‘And the men who were with me did not see it.’”

This is entirely one with the aforementioned triad. Prophecy is the true teaching in the Revelation of E. <note>Possibly referring to Elijah or Ezekiel.</note> The Holy Spirit is here the **Old Testament**, just as it was taught outwardly among the pious, who nevertheless attained their measure of the Spirit from it. The **Bath Kol**, or Daughter of the Voice, is the **New Testament**, just as it was taught outwardly among the pious, who attained their measure of the Spirit from it. These are the 3 parts of prophecy, and absolutely nothing else.

# Chapter 4.

## On Paradise.

### § I.

Paradise is called by the Rabbis <term>Gan Eden <note>original: "גן עדן", Hebrew for Garden of Eden</note></term>, the Garden of Eden, which means as much as a garden of delight and pleasure. In the Church, it represents the true doctrine in the Revelation of C. <note>likely referring to the Book of Revelation</note>; in Nature, however, it is the state of blessing of the earth, which is again twofold; the upper world is also called a Garden of Eden, about all of which more will be seen in what follows.

Rabbi Eliezer in the <term>Pirke <note>Referring to the "Pirke De-Rabbi Eliezer," an 8th-century midrashic work on the Torah.</note></term>, chapter 3, says: That Paradise was one of the seven things that God created even before the creation of this world. The words are as follows:
> "Seven things were created before the world was created,
"and these are: the Law, Hell, Paradise, the Throne of Glory,
"the Sanctuary, or the Temple, Repentance or turning back, and
"the name of the Messiah." As proof of Paradise, he says: "because Genesis
"2:8 says: And the Lord God planted a garden in Eden
" <term>Mikedem <note>original: "מקדם", a Hebrew word usually translated as "eastward," but interpreted by the author and certain traditions as "from the beginning" or "of old."</note></term> from eternity, before the world was created."

The world is the Church, and the Church is twofold: as the outer Church, which is called *this world*; and the universal Church, which is called *the world to come*. Before the outer Church-world, God wrote the Law—namely, the entire Word of God. He also made the Satanic nature as Hell. Likewise, he created the earth in the beginning into a Paradise. His Word was also a Paradise, a temple, a throne of glory, upon which the Son of Man shall sit and judge, and in which the Messiah lies described. In the letter <note>A reference to the "dead letter" or literal level of scripture, as opposed to its spirit.</note>, however, it was also Hell and death; and repentance or turning back from error to truth was also already prepared therein, as were the punishments of Hell. All of this was determined before it came to pass, and our redemption from corruption was determined before we entered into it. But in the beginning, repentance or turning back was not yet actually prepared or created; therefore, we must now also take the world as the Kingdom of Christ, through which we find the full meaning of these things.
