Before God creates the new world of the Kingdom of Christ, he establishes the true law in the doctrine of the <term>Revelation of C. <note>Likely "Offenbarung Christi," or the Revelation of Christ/Book of Revelation.</note></term>, which is itself Paradise, the Throne of Glory, and the new Temple: and here he creates the Messiah, who is to sit and judge upon this throne. Here the garden in Eden is planted <term>mikkedem <note>original: "מקדם", a Hebrew word meaning both "from the east" and "from of old."</note></term>, from the morning, which is to say, out of the true doctrine of the <term>O.T. <note>Old Testament</note></term>; for the Old Testament is to be regarded as the morning in comparison to the <term>N.T. <note>New Testament</note></term>. *Mikkedem* also means "from eternity," because the Kingdom of Christ, which is built with this doctrine, is called an eternal kingdom, for there shall be no more death or dying within it. Here the beginning shall be in the end, as the end of the world will once again be equal to the initial Paradise, and because the "Hell" of the time experienced thus far existed before this new world. Because the "world" is the Church, and the Church is twofold; so must all these things that were said to have existed before the world be understood as twofold. Thus, we are directed toward the twofold doctrine of the Word of God—namely the inner and the outer doctrine—whereby the outer doctrine, in a certain light, is also called a Paradise that preceded the future new world, as we shall see in what follows.

§. 2. The great <term>Jalkut Rubeni <note>A 17th-century collection of Kabbalistic midrashim by Rabbi Reuben Hoeshke.</note></term> says, <note>original: "fol. 41. col. 2. in Parascha Vajera"</note> folio 41, column 2, in the section Vayera: *Know that the lower Paradise was created 1365 years before the lower world in which we now exist.* To be able to state the actual meaning of this, one would need to have the book itself and read the entire context of what precedes and follows. However, since I do not possess the book myself, I can say nothing more of it than what is visible from these few words. In the doctrine, the "lower world" is the outer Church, and before it existed, the earth was a Paradise. The numbers are not to be understood according to the literal letter, as any person of understanding can easily judge. The two Churches under the two Testaments are also two "worlds," and in this regard, the Christian Church is the lower world. The number 1365, in this sense, indicates the preceding time in general, back to the initial Paradise.

The book <term>Bereschith rabba <note>Genesis Rabbah, a classical homiletic commentary on the Book of Genesis.</note></term>, <note>original: "fol. 21. col. 1. Parascha 21"</note> folio 21, column 1, section 21, says: *Hell was created before Paradise; specifically, Hell on the 2nd day, and Paradise on the 3rd day.* Here, the focus is on the two Testaments and the doctrine of the Revelation of C. The second Testament, as the New Testament with the Christian Church, was the second day and "Hell." And the true doctrine following it, with the Kingdom of Christ, is "Paradise." <term>R. Mosche bar Nachmann <note>Also known as Nachmanides or Ramban, a leading medieval Jewish scholar.</note></term> says the exact same thing in <term>Torath Adam <note>The Law of Man, a work by Nachmanides covering the laws of mourning and the afterlife.</note></term>, folio 98, column 1.

## The Nature of Paradise.

§. 3. *Rabbi Moses ben Maimon* <note>Commonly known as Maimonides (1135–1204), a preeminent Sephardic Jewish philosopher and scholar.</note>, regarding *Mishna Sanhedrin* <note>A tractate of the Talmud dealing with judicial matters and the afterlife.</note>, *folio 119, column 1*, says: "One group holds that the Good is Paradise: and that it is a place where they eat and drink without labor of the body and without toil; and that in that place there are houses of precious stones and beds prepared of silk; and that rivers flow there of wine and fragrant oil, and many such things besides. Another group holds and considers that the expected Good would be the 'Days of the Messiah' <note>The Messianic Age</note>, who would be revealed in haste; and that at that same time all children of Adam would become as angels, and would have many children and multiply so that they would inhabit the whole world forever and ever. Likewise, that the Messiah, according to their thoughts, would remain alive with the help of the blessed God: and that in those same days the earth would bring forth woven clothes and baked bread, and many such things besides, which are impossible." Namely, according to the letter, it is impossible that the earth should bring forth woven clothes and baked bread, which is precisely what should lead us to another meaning.

Great mysteries are spoken here quite openly, yet they are covered up again by being spoken of as the opinions of different parties. The first is that one will live in Paradise without labor and toil. The eating and drinking, the houses and beds, and the streams of wine and oil, are intended to refer to the **Doctrine of Wisdom**. The other is that this glorious Paradise shall exist in the days of the Messiah and will come with him, and that he will be revealed in haste upon the whole earth once the 'Beast with the abomination of desolation' <note>A reference to Biblical prophecy, specifically from Daniel and Matthew, often associated with the end times.</note> first arrives. Along with this, it is also said that one must understand 'angels' to mean humans, because all humans in the Kingdom of *Christ* are to be angels; consequently, the godless, by contrast, are also called 'devils.' The great multiplication of children refers to the spiritual multiplication in the true doctrine, which shall occupy and inhabit the entire earth. Furthermore, it is stated here publicly that the Messiah will not die, and consequently all other people who come into this kingdom will not die either, for at the end of it they pass over through transformation into an even greater glory. *1 Corinthians 15:51; 1 Thessalonians 4:15.*

## Two Paradises.

§. 4. The book *Megalle Ammykkoth* <note>original: "Megalleh Amukot" (Revealer of Depths), a 17th-century Kabbalistic work by Nathan Nata Spira.</note>, *folio 78, column 2, Section 223*, says: Just as there is a paradise above in heaven, so also there is a paradise below on earth.

The upper world alone has two Paradises: the Upper with the fixed stars, and the Lower with the planets. Likewise, the lower world on earth has two successive Paradises: the first with the radiant earth, and the second with the middle state, which now reappears for the first time with the Kingdom of Christ. Now, when the upper world and the lower world are held against one another, the two above are taken as one, and so also the two below. In this way, there is one Paradise above in heaven, and one below on earth. Furthermore, the Kingdom of Christ is also called heaven, and the outer church is called the earth; and thus, in this consideration, the outer church is called the lower Paradise, and the true doctrine along with the Kingdom of Christ is called the upper Paradise. Likewise, the Old Testament is compared to heaven, and the New Testament to the earth, and so both are also taken as two Paradises. It all lies in the comparison, and one must pay heed to which things God’s Word sets in comparison to one another. For when one has the one, the other—as its counterpart—is soon found.

Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel in *Nishmat Hayyim* <note>original: "Nischmath chajim" — "The Breath of Life," a 1651 work on the immortality of the soul</note>, folio 25, column 2, chapter 10, Treatise I, says:

The one is the Upper Palace, and therein are rivers of balsam, and all sorts of delights of the future life."

This should be understood as the Kingdom of Christ, and also as the Upper World.
> "The Lower Paradise, however, which is called the Lower Palace, also has something of the delights of the future life: It has nothing of itself, however, until it is given to it from the Upper Palace, and it is called *Appiryon* <note>A Hebrew term for a palanquin or bridal canopy, often associated with the Chariot or the union of the soul with God</note>, that is, a bridal bed."

When the Kingdom of Christ is taken as the Lower Paradise, this indicates the special connection of the lower world with the upper world, as heaven is, as it were, reunited with the earth: for without this, no such Paradise could exist on earth. The primary meaning, however, refers to doctrine; the outer doctrine of the Word of God is the Lower Paradise. This also contains some delights of the future life within it. But it has nothing of itself in the literal <term>letter</term> <note>The "letter" refers to the literal, surface-level reading of scripture, which requires the "spirit" for true understanding.</note> until it is given to it from the Upper Palace, from the spirit of the inner true doctrine. This palace is the outer bridal bed, where the church has united with God in the outer doctrine. ### Where Paradise May Be in the World?

§. 5. Rabbi Shem Tov, in his *Sefer Ha-Emunot* <note>original: "Sepher haëmunoth" — "The Book of Beliefs," a 14th-century work by Shem Tov ibn Shem Tov</note>, folio 65, column 1, chapter 6, Gate 6, says: "It is clear from the words of the scholars of the Scripture that Paradise is found in this world at a certain place on the earth, and that four rivers go out from it, one of which is the Euphrates <note>original: "Phrath" — the Hebrew name for the river Euphrates</note>, which surrounds the Land of Israel. The Euphrates is named alone to indicate that the Paradise of the true doctrine shall emerge again from the Christian Church—which is the Euphrates—for the doctrine of Christ includes all nations within itself, and thus flows around the Land of Israel, because everything shall be gathered into one under the name of Jesus. Beneath this line lies Paradise along with the Kingdom of Christ, in which there will no longer be any increasing or decreasing of the day, but rather an everlasting day: of which the Middle Line, which makes day and night equal, is taken as a symbol. It is therefore a certain place in the world where Paradise is. To be sure, it is everywhere in the inner true doctrine among all peoples; but it is nonetheless specifically and preeminently in the Church under the name of Jesus. In the same way, in nature, the whole earth will be a Paradise; but preeminently and quite specifically it will be in the Jewish land around Jerusalem, which shall then also be the center of the earth, as all this is proven in the *Book of the World*.

# On Paradise.

“...rejoice the elders.” According to the testimony of the two Testaments <note>The Old and New Testaments of the Bible.</note>, we progress from strength to strength, from power to power, and from one clarity to another. Now, because the entire world, along with the outer church, has been arranged so specifically into a trinity <note>original: "Drey-zahl"</note>; it is therefore in accordance with the harmony of all things that the people in the Kingdom of Christ shall also progress through three stages from strength to strength, and from knowledge to knowledge: for it is impossible to be transported from the current great darkness into the greatest light without intermediate steps. Further:

“There are also in Paradise eighty <term>ribos</term> <note>original: "80 Ribos"; a Hebrew term for ten thousand, thus totaling 800,000.</note> species of trees in all its corners, and the least among them is more praiseworthy than all balsam trees. In every corner there are also eighty <term>ribos</term> serving angels who sing with a lovely voice: and the Tree of Life is in the center, whose branches cover the whole of Paradise.” Hitherto, death and corruption were in all things, but there, the holy power of God will penetrate all things in the whole of nature on earth, and take death and corruption captive, so that there will be no more death, suffering, nor pain: and that is the Tree of Life, which stands in the midst of all trees and covers the whole of Paradise—the whole earth—with its branches.

“It also has five hundred thousand flavors, and none is equal to the other. There are likewise seven clouds of glory above it, and it is moved from the four sides of the world, so that its fragrance goes from one end of the world to the other. Beneath it,” namely under the Tree of Life, “are the disciples of the wise who explain the Law, and each has two coverings, one of stars and the other of the sun and moon, and between each covering is a curtain of the clouds of glory.” Here we see once again that our occupation will be with the Word of God, which in its true sense is also the Tree of Life that will be moved in all four main religions. We shall find the outer and inner, the temporal and eternal described therein, which are the two coverings. We shall see the secrets of God and the whole world, and that will be our joy and lovely pastime, as indeed in a natural way there can be no other joy or occupation in eternity. The priests <note>original: "Pfaffen"; a derogatory term for clergy, implying they are superstitious or unlearned in true spiritual matters.</note> certainly say that the beholding of God would be the eternal joy, but how and what that may be, they themselves know nothing of it—so beautifully have they studied in the Law of God! From their teachings there is nothing further to be learned than that the beholding of God would be like the way a cow stares at a new barn door <note>A German idiom meaning to look at something with total incomprehension or blankness.</note>; for the cow knows just as much about what the barn door is as the priest knows what God is. What joy would there be in that?

# Of Paradise.

“The field is with me.” <note>A reference to Psalm 50:11: "I know all the birds of the mountains, and the creatures of the field are mine."</note> The *Targum* <note>An ancient Aramaic translation and paraphrase of the Hebrew Bible</note> renders these words thus:
> “The *Tarnegol* <note>Hebrew for rooster/cock</note> or Field Cock, whose shins are on the earth but whose head reaches to the heavens, sings before me.”

This bird represents the outer doctrine of the Islamic Church, and thereby all outer doctrine. The Old Testament is the Heaven, and in it the Islamic Church has its head and its strength; therefore, the head reaches to the heavens. But the New Testament is the Earth, upon which this Church stands with its feet. The water of its doctrine was so fast and strongly flowing that the nature of the true doctrine could find no ground nor rest. Therefore, the voice—the *Bath Kol* <note>Literally "daughter of a voice," meaning a divine echo or heavenly proclamation</note>, which belongs primarily to the New Testament—cried out: "Do not descend into it, into the doctrine of the Old Testament; for seven years ago a man dropped an axe therein, and it has not yet reached the bottom." <note>This suggests the literal or outward interpretation of the law is a bottomless pit or an unfathomable depth that distracts from the spirit.</note>

He is called *Sis* <note>The Ziz, a giant mythological bird in Jewish tradition, often paired with Leviathan and Behemoth</note> in the field, of which *Rabbi Solomon Jarchi* <note>Better known as Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval commentator on the Torah and Talmud</note> says: The name זיז *Sis* is from זוו *Sus*, to move; and the animals of the field are called *Sis* because they move from one place to another.

*Vajikra Rabba* <note>A homiletic midrash (commentary) on the book of Leviticus</note>, Section 22, folio 155, column 4, as also *Rabbi David Kimchi* <note>A medieval rabbi and grammarian known as Radak</note> says in the *Book of Roots* <note>original: "Sepher haschoreschim"</note> regarding the word *Sis*:
> *Rabbi Judah*, the son of *Simon*, says: When he spreads his wings, he darkens the sphere of the sun; and this is meant when Job 39:26 says: *Is it by your wisdom that the hawk flies and spreads his wings toward the south?*

Here we see that the Islamic Church is meant by this, for it is symbolized by the south <note>The German "Mittag" translates both as "noon" and "south," the direction of the Islamic world relative to Europe</note> and also dwells toward the south. It has grown in size and strength beyond all other religions, and has thus darkened the sphere or circle of the sun—that is, the outward doctrine of the entire Church of all other nations. The *Sis*, the Field Cock, and the Hawk are thus all three one and the same; and that the bird *Sis* signifies an outward doctrine is clear from the fact that the hawk is counted among the unclean birds in Leviticus 11.

Furthermore, it is asked in the aforementioned place: Why is he called *Sis*? Answer: Because he has many kinds of tastes from this and that. See also *Aben Esra* <note>Abraham ibn Ezra (1089–1167), a polymath and biblical commentator</note> on Daniel 12:3.

By these "many kinds of tastes," the mixture of the doctrine of the Islamic Church is indicated, for it has mixed together doctrines from the Christians, Jews, and Heathens; therefore, it is also the peacock with its colorful feathers. Indeed, for this very reason, this Church is positioned as a middle-point, through which in the end all religions shall be brought into one.

# Of Paradise.

The Talmud, Tractate Berachoth, folio 57, column 2, says the following of the bird Bar Juchne <note>A mythical giant bird in Jewish folklore, often identified with the Ziz</note> or Sis: "Once, an egg of the Bar Juchne fell; it flooded sixty cities and shattered three hundred cedar trees." And how could this be? Did the bird simply cast it away? For it is written in Job 39:13: "The wing of the *Renanim* <note>original: רננים; often translated as peacocks or ostriches</note> is joyful." To this, Rabbi Ashi spoke: "That same egg was useless and rotten."

The three hundred cedars represent the external teachings of the three religions—the Christians, Jews, and Heathens—which were shattered by the egg, signifying the doctrine of the Islamic Church <note>The original text uses "Mohamedanische Kirche"</note>. The sixty cities represent the same, and the number six points to the six working days of the outward matters of faith of these three religions, which have been overwhelmed by the Turkish Church. This was thus a mighty egg, but it was nonetheless rotten and useless; therefore, this bird must also be slaughtered and killed if the righteous are to reach their great banquet.

The word <term>Renanim</term> <note>original: רננים; meaning "joyful shouts" or "singing birds"</note> signifies a peacock, as it is also used in Job 39:13. The root word of it is <term>Ranan</term> <note>original: רנן; to sing, cry out, or rejoice</note>, to sing or shout, as peacocks are prone to do. The Turkish Church could also be joyful and sing because of its successful and vast expansion.

Sammael <note>In Jewish tradition, an archangel who often functions as the accuser or the personification of evil</note> makes himself very bold here by mocking this bird. For all of these are indeed one and the same.

<term>Rashi</term> <note>Solomon ben Isaac (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval Jewish commentator on the Bible and Talmud</note> says: These are the portions which the righteous would receive at the great banquet in the world to come.

<term>Samael</term> <note>In Jewish tradition, Samael is often an accuser or angel of death; here, the author refers to a specific source or figure mocking these traditions</note> has only extracted this matter in fragments, therefore I can say nothing specific about it. ### The Old Wine at the Final Banquet.

§. 19. The <term>Talmud</term> <note>The central text of Rabbinic Judaism</note>, Tractate <term>Sanhedrin</term>, folio 99, column 1, says of this:
> "What do the words mean: 'No eye has seen it,' <note>original: "Kein Aug hat es gesehen"</note> Isaiah 64:4? Rabbi Joshua ben Levi <note>original: "Jehoscha der Sohn Levi"</note> says: They mean the wine which has been kept preserved in its grapes since the six days of Creation."

The six days of Creation here represent the entire period of the formation of the outward Church through the outward teaching of the Word of God. And the true inner doctrine is the old wine, which has been kept preserved within the outward teaching until the end, when the righteous in the Kingdom of Christ shall drink this wine. Certainly no eye has ever seen this doctrine in the Book of Revelation <note>original: "Off. C."; referring to the Apocalypse of John</note>, and consequently, neither has it seen the things described therein.

The <term>Targum</term> <note>An Aramaic translation and paraphrase of the Hebrew Bible</note> on the Song of Solomon 8:2 says of this:

And <term>Shulchan Arba</term> <note>original: "Schylchan arba"; a work by the Kabbalist Bahya ben Asher concerning the mystical significance of meals</note>, folio 9, column 2, says:
> "The excellence of these same foods is very great for sharpening the understanding and purifying the heart, just as the <term>Manna</term> <note>The miraculous food provided to the Israelites in the desert</note> did, of which the generation of the wilderness was worthy; it was like a cake with honey and came from the highest light."

Here you Jews can see that the old wine is a new doctrine [drawn] from the outward literal teaching, and that the Messiah brings and teaches this doctrine. These teachings are also the foods of pomegranates and fruits, which sharpen the understanding of the Word of God and purify the heart. One religion also considers itself righteous and the other wicked and unrighteous: it regards its own doctrine as a "good day," and the doctrine of the others as an "evil day." ## How the Souls of the Righteous are Received in Paradise.

§. 22. <term>Nischmath Chajim<gloss>Hebrew for "The Breath of Life," a 17th-century work by Rabbi Menasseh ben Israel regarding the soul and the afterlife.</gloss></term>, folio 28, column 1, chapter 10, Treatise 1, says of this:

In the spiritual teaching, this has the following meaning: The inhabitants of Paradise are those who are already established in the teaching of the <term>Off. C.<gloss>An abbreviation likely for "Offenbarung Christi" (The Revelation of Christ), representing an inner, mystical understanding of faith.</gloss></term>. When someone comes anew from the outer teaching into the true teaching, they rejoice and receive them with a friendly countenance, especially if they are **relatives, friends**, and **like-minded** companions. The outer teaching is very far removed from the true teaching, and thus they come from a very distant land. Here they converse about things and tell one another what a glorious thing the higher wisdom of the Word of God is, compared to the wretched priestly wisdom in the outer church! ## Of Hell and Purgatory.

->§. 1.<-

Just as Paradise is manifold, and the inner doctrine is also called a Paradise; even so is Hell also manifold, and the external priestly doctrine <note>original: "Pfaffen-Lehre"; a derogatory term for the established church’s teachings.</note> and this current age of corruption are called a Hell. Sammael <note>The author's nickname for his opponent.</note> has merely extracted those things regarding Hell from the Talmud and from the Rabbis which seemed most suitable to him for presenting the Rabbis and the Jews as objects of mockery and laughter; we, however, wish to see what is actually meant by these things.

### Where Hell may be.

The book *Zioni* <note>Refers to the *Sefer ha-Zioni*, a 14th-century Kabbalistic commentary on the Pentateuch by Menahem Zioni.</note>, folio 2, column 2, *Parashat Bereshit* <note>The first weekly Torah portion, covering Genesis 1:1–6:8.</note>, says: "Paradise and Hell border one another, and a wall divides them; Paradise is on the Northeast side, according to Psalm 17:14, where it is said: *With your North <note>The author is likely following a specific interpretation of the Hebrew "hidden store" (tsephun-ka) as "North."</note> you fill their belly.* On the Northwest side, however, is Hell; and a spring goes out from Paradise, but the spring which comes from Hell is hot."

The matter concerns doctrine. The Old Testament is the East or the Morning, and the New Testament with the Christian church is the West or the Evening, and it is also the North or Midnight <note>In early modern German, "Mitternacht" (Midnight) was a standard term for the direction of North.</note>, just as the Christian church inhabits the Northern part of the world. The doctrine of the O. C. <note>likely "Offenbahrtes Christenthum" (Revealed Christianity), a common reference in Radical Pietist literature.</note> is thus Paradise on the Northeastern side, because it rises out of the Old Testament and within the Christian church, and also toward the North. But the Antichrist with his doctrine of *Maozim* <note>original: "Måusims Lehre"; a reference to the "god of fortresses" in Daniel 11:38, often used by reformers to describe the papacy or worldly church power.</note> is the Hell on the Northwestern side, because he likewise comes out of the Christian church, as well as from the hellish influence of Satan, 2 Thessalonians 2, Revelation 9:1 and following. Thus the O. C. and the Antichrist—Paradise and Hell—are together in one place, and only a wall divides them.

The satanic nature also has the greatest power on the Northern side; therefore, the Antichrist and Destroyer comes from the Christian church and from no other. On the Northern side, he also sets himself against the holy mountain of the O. C., and leads from there to Hell, Isaiah 14:14, 15. The word <term>Zaphon <gloss>צפון; Hebrew for North</gloss></term> means North or Midnight,

This is what is meant here by the words: *With your North you fill their belly*, which also means: *With your hidden treasure you fill their belly.* <note>The author is playing on the Hebrew word *Zaphon* (North), which shares a root with *Zaphan* (to hide or treasure up). §. 2. The book *Thorath Adam* <note>Hebrew: *Torat Ha-Adam* ("The Law of Man"), a work by the 13th-century scholar Nachmanides.</note>, folio 102, column 3, the chapter titled *Schaar haggemul* <note>Hebrew: *Sha'ar ha-Gemul* ("The Gate of Reward"), which discusses eschatology, suffering, and the afterlife.</note>, says: In the *Medrasch Koheleth* <note>The Midrash on the book of Ecclesiastes.</note> it is asked: Why did the Holy God create "Hell and Paradise?" Answer: "So that one might "be saved through the other. But how much space is there between them? Rabbi Jochanan "says: There is a wall between them. But Rabbi Acha says: There is a hand- "breadth between them. Our Rabbis, however, say: Two fingers."

The doctrine of the Word of God is the wall, the hand, and—in the two Testaments—the two fingers. Inwardly it is Paradise, and outwardly it is Hell; and thus the intervening space is only a wall, a hand-breadth, and two fingers wide. The literal doctrine <note>original: "Buchstaben-Lehre"; refers to a surface-level, legalistic interpretation of scripture.</note> must also help to save one from the external yoke, as one thing toffles the other: and the Antichrist must also help to save, in that he must lay waste to the priestly-whore. <note>A derogatory term common in radical Pietist writings for the corrupt institutional church or "Babel."</note> Thus, one saves through the other. The true doctrine saves through the literal doctrine by breaking one literal image with another: and God breaks one devil through another. Regarding this, one may also read *Nischmath Chajim* <note>Hebrew: *Nishmat Chayyim* ("The Breath of Life") by Menasseh ben Israel, a 17th-century work on the soul.</note>, folio 31, column 1, chapter 12, part 1, and *Medrasch Koheleth* folio 127, column 1, on Ecclesiastes 7:14, where it says: *God has made the one as well as the other*, which words are meant to suggest: that Paradise and Hell are, as it were, equal to one another, so that one can look from one into the other. This refers to the doctrine of the Word of God, which in its true sense is a Paradise, but in the "letter of contention" <note>The argumentative, literal interpretation.</note> is a Hell. In the same way, the very same essence and mind of a human being can become a devil and a Hell, or an angel and a Paradise. Furthermore, in the future, the blessed and the damned shall see one another. Through these beautiful images, we are thus taught that one should not seek Heaven and Hell as places so far distant from one another, but rather seek them within oneself, within the Church on earth itself, and within the nature on earth in which we live.

## The Names of Hell. <term>Gehinom<gloss>Gehenna</gloss></term>.

<margin>folio 14. column 2.</margin>
§. 3. Regarding the cause of this name, *Rabbi Elias* <note>original: "Rabbi Elias in Tischbi". Referring to Elijah Levita (1469–1549), a Hebrew lexicographer whose work *Tishbi* explains Talmudic and Rabbinic vocabulary.</note> says the following in *Tishbi*: "Our Rabbis, of blessed memory, have named the place in "which the godless are punished after their death *Gehinom*, "namely the Valley of *Hinnom*, "because the Valley of the Son of *Hinnom*, which lay near "to *Jerusalem*, was a foul place where they "burned their children to *Moloch*. <margin>2 Kings 23:10.</margin> It was, however, named thus because the "child howls and cries there."

<margin>Doctrine of the Rev. C.,</margin>
At the end of the outward Church is the judgment, where the godless are punished. *Jerusalem*, near which the Valley of *Hinnom* is located, represents at its end the doctrine of the <term>Rev. C.<gloss>Revelation of Christ</gloss></term>, and yet it is also the Christian Church in which these things take place. *Moloch* is the Antichrist with his <term>Mausim<gloss>Maozim</gloss></term> <note>A reference to Daniel 11:38, the "god of forces" or "fortresses," often interpreted by mystical writers as the false idols or worldly powers supported by the Antichrist.</note>, to whom they sacrifice and burn their children, their faith, and their teachings of the Word of God. Therefore, it is a foul place where the godless—who must die to the outward doctrine here—are punished after this death of theirs. Here there will be enough howling and crying, for which reason it is named so here. This is thus the Hell that is near to Paradise, namely near the *Revelation of Christ* and also near the Kingdom of Christ. The name *Moloch* means a king, and points to the kings who will create this Hell. Hell after death will, of course, also be named thus, and it is also foul enough. In the outward Christian Church, the <term>clerical regime<gloss>original: "Pfaffen-Regiment"</gloss></term> <note>The author uses the derogatory term "Pfaffe" for priests to criticize the established church hierarchy.</note> was the *Moloch*, for their articles of faith were strife, hatred, and bitterness toward others. When the children of the Church were led into these doctrines of strife, they were sacrificed and burned to *Moloch*, for from this arose religious wars, murder, singeing, and burning. The Valley of *Hinnom* is thus always near *Jerusalem*, that is, within the Christian Church. This was a Hell into which Christ also entered and preached to the spirits in prison, for He was indeed present with His Word and Spirit in this Church; and next to His temple, the clerical devil built a chapel.

It is called *Sheol* according to Jonah 2:2: *I cried out of the belly of Sheol or Hell, and you heard my voice.* This is the captivity...

## The Measure of Hell.

§. 6. In the <term>Talmud, Tractate Taanit</term> <note>A volume of the Talmud dealing with fast days; the reference is to folio 10a.</note> folio 10, column 1, it is said: that Hell is 60 times larger than Paradise. See also <term>Rabbi Gedaliah</term> in his <term>Shalshelet Ha-Kabbalah</term> <note>Meaning "The Chain of Tradition," a 16th-century work of Jewish history and lore.</note> folio 86, column 1. Likewise, <term>Torat HaAdam</term> <note>original: "Torath adum". This is Nahmanides' "The Law of Man," a 13th-century work on mourning and the afterlife.</note>, folio 96, column 4, under the title <term>Sha'ar Ha-Gemul</term> <note>Meaning "The Gate of Reward," a section discussing the world to come.</note>.

The outer teaching is called death and hell, as is clear from Isaiah 28:15-18. The six workdays or six periods of the outer church and teaching are thus this measure of Hell, which is 60 times larger than the true teaching with the seventh period of the Kingdom of Christ. The entire time until now is called a hell because the satanic nature worked powerfully and strongly within it; and where Satan is, there is also a hell. This time is indeed much longer than the Kingdom of Christ; therefore, in respect to the six days of creation compared to the seventh day of rest, it is held to be a ratio of 60 to 1. It is also the case that far more people have gone to Hell than are saved, for the way to Hell was broad, and many walked upon it; whereas the way to life was narrow, and few walked upon it, as Christ says in Matthew 7:15. Now, because Hell is compared with the six days of creation, it also follows that the satanic nature has had to serve the process of creation on earth until now.

## Hell belongs among the six days' work of Creation.

§. 8. ## On the Gates of Hell.

§. 14. The *Yalkut Shimoni* <note>A significant medieval midrashic compilation that collects various interpretations of the Hebrew Bible.</note> regarding Isaiah, folio 46, column 1, number 296, sets the number of the gates of Hell at 8,000, and says: "At the time of redemption, God will say the following words to the angels Michael and Gabriel: 'Open the gates of Hell, and bring them up!' Then they will immediately go with the keys and open the 8,000 gates of Hell."

Michael and Gabriel represent the spirit within the true teaching of the two Testaments <note>The Old and New Testaments.</note>. The teachings found in the **dead letter** <note>A reference to literalist, legalistic interpretations of scripture that lack spiritual vitality.</note> are the gates of Hell, according to Isaiah 28:16, 18. These gates were previously closed, so that one could not recognize them as the gates of Hell; but now they are being opened through the true teaching of the **Revelation of Christ**, so that one can see the **priest-hell** with all its inhabitants. The number 8 is a number that indicates the external state in conflict and in division, just as do the numbers 4 and 2. The little book *Otiyot* <note>Likely referring to the *Otiyot de-Rabbi Akiva*, an esoteric work on the Hebrew alphabet.</note>, folio 15, column 4, and folio 16, column 1, therefore sets the number of such gates as high as 40,000.

The *Yalkut Reuveni* <note>A 17th-century collection of Kabbalistic midrashim.</note>, number 1, under the title *Metzullah* <note>meaning "The Depths"</note> from the book *Midrash Neelam* <note>The "Hidden Midrash," a portion of the Zohar.</note>, folio 48, column 1 and 2, speaks of 50 gates, as follows:

> In Hell there are 50 gates which are completely full of holes, and the feet of the godless are stuck in these same holes, and they cry out: "O, woe unto our feet!"

The number 50 is a number of the interior, and points toward the opening of the hellish gates through the true teaching. In this, the godless first receive their "Woe," which they did not feel before, but here they shall feel it.

The book *Emek HaMelekh* <note>"The Valley of the King," a 17th-century Kabbalistic work by Naftali Herz Bacharach.</note>, folio 144, column 2, chapter 35, sets only 7 gates and 7 dwellings in Hell. Likewise, in *Pirkei De-Rabbi Eliezer*, chapter 43. These 7 gates are one and the same as the 7 dwellings that have already been explained above.

The Talmud, tractate *Eruvin*, folio 19, column 1, sets 3 gates, and says: one is in the desert, one in the sea, and one in Jerusalem. For the gate in the sea, the words of Jonah 2:3 are applied: "I cried out of the belly of Hell, and you heard my voice." Regarding the gate in Jerusalem, the words from Isaiah 31:9 are interpreted: "Thus speaks the Lord, who has a fire in Zion and a hearth in Jerusalem." Rabbi Ishmael says: Hell itself would be indicated by the words: "He who has his fire in Zion."

## Various Punishments of the Hells.

## Of the Origin of the Hellish Fire.

§. 16. The Rabbis say: The fire of the lower Hell originates from the fire of the upper Hell. See *Nishmat Chayim* <note>original: "Nischmath chajim," meaning "The Breath of Life," a treatise on the soul by Menasseh ben Israel.</note> folio 34, columns 1 and 2, chapter 13, Treatise I. The lower Hell is the Hell of this present time within the external nature on Earth, because the satanic nature operates above the Earth in the air. This satanic fire above the Earth comes from the satanic fire within the Earth, which is the upper Hell. In a <term>lightning strike (Wetterschlag)</term> is the satanic nature, which causes the ignition; therefore the fire of a thunderbolt is so fierce and penetrating that it melts any metal it hits in an instant. But here it is still not nearly as fierce as it is in itself and within the Earth, because it is still tempered and weakened by the spirit of the external nature above the Earth.

Gold and silver cannot be destroyed by external fire, nor can other physical things be entirely annihilated, for the ash and the salt still remain behind. But the satanic nature, as the hellish fire, destroys gold and silver, stones and rocks, earth, and all coarse physical matter in an instant, so completely that not the slightest bit of it remains; and indeed it happens as quickly and in an instant as a metal is melted by a lightning strike. This is the fire of the Last Judgment, which at the end of the Kingdom of Christ will swallow and destroy the entire coarse Earth with all coarse physical things in an instant, including the coarseness of the bodies of the faithful. These people, however, pass through this fire without feeling anything, because the core of their physicality is permeated and <term>tinctured (tingiret)</term> <note>An alchemical term meaning to be deeply infused with a spiritual quality that transforms the essence of a substance.</note> with the life of God, so that only the coarse essence is taken away, and the body itself remains standing in clarity. This is the transformation at the end of the Kingdom of Christ, 1 Corinthians 15:51. And this happens as the satanic nature above the Earth is driven away into the Earth. See, you blasphemous priests, you must go into this fire, and it will drag you into the abyss with it! One might perhaps say that this is far too unmerciful, for it—

Bechai," referring to Bahya ben Asher, a 13th-century scholar.</note> on the Five Books of Moses, folio 220, in **Torah Portion Nitzavim** <note>original: "Parascha Nizzabim," referring to Deuteronomy 29:9–30:20.</note> says: "Solomon understood the two daughters of the leech <note>original: "Blut-Igel." This refers to the 'horse-leech' mentioned in Proverbs 30:15.</note> to be the two nations of the **Christians** and **Mohammedans**, Proverbs 30, 15, and compared Hell, as the place of judgment and the punishment of the godless, to a leech which draws out the blood—namely, the soul."

These two regimes and nations have the greatest power and dominion over the entire earth, and Jews and Heathens have been pressed and oppressed by them. They are therefore rightly compared to leeches, for they have not only taken the true meaning—as the life and the soul—from the Word of God; but they have also spread their religions through bloodshed, murder, and robbery. The Heathens did not do such things, and had no need to, because before their church there was no other that they would have had to conquer; the Jews could not do it, for they never possessed worldly power. Thus, it is only the two last primary religions, the Christians and Mohammedans, who are the two daughters of the leech.

Of these two nations, the Rabbis say that Isaiah 66:17 also speaks, where it says: **Those who sanctify and purify themselves in the gardens.** The words "those who sanctify themselves" refer to the **children of Edom** <note>A traditional Jewish designation for the Roman Empire and, by extension, Christendom.</note>, as the Christians. The words "those who purify themselves," however, refer to the **Ishmaelites**, as the Mohammedans. The custom of the children of Edom would be: To move the fingers back and forth, namely when the Christians make the sign of the cross; the Ishmaelites, however, only wash their hands and feet, but not their hearts; that is, they strictly observe their outward teachings and ceremonies. Further:

Among those who eat swine's flesh, the children of Edom, as the Christians, are meant. But among those who eat abominations and mice, the Ishmaelites or Mohammedans would be understood. See also **Kad ha-Kemach** <note>original: "Cad hakkemach," a treatise on ethics by Bahya ben Asher.</note>, folio 20, column 1. Likewise, in the book **Otiot** <note>original: "Othioth," likely "Otiot de-Rabbi Akiva," an esoteric midrash on the alphabet.</note>, folio 15, column 2, 3. Likewise, **Rabbi Joseph ben Yahya** on Psalm 140:11.

These are God’s own interpretations and meanings, upon which one can rely. One also sees from this that the repetitions of things, where two or more speeches of the same content follow one another, also include as many nations or religions, although everything is also meant for each one, and each for all.

## Hell is primarily for the Christians, and Paradise for the Jews or Israelites.

§. 24. This is primarily discussed by **Rabbi Bahya** <note>original: "R. Bechai," referring to Bahya ben Asher, a 13th-century Spanish scholar and Kabbalist.</note> in his commentary on the Five Books of Moses, folio 34, column 4, in **Torah Portion Toldot** <note>original: "Parascha Toledoth," the section of Genesis 25:19–28:9 covering the birth of Esau and Jacob.</note>, as well as in **Bereshit Rabbah** <note>A collection of ancient rabbinic interpretations of Genesis.</note>, folio 60, column 1, Portion 65. The book **Tzeror HaMor** <note>original: "Zeror hammor," a commentary by Abraham Saba.</note>, folio 27, column 1, in the portion "Toldot Yitzhak," says: Esau the godless has no portion in the world to come.

**Abarbanel** <note>Isaac Abarbanel (1437–1508), a prominent Jewish statesman and philosopher.</note> in his work *Mashmia Yeshu'ah* <note>original: "Maschmiah Jeschua," translating to "The Announcer of Salvation."</note>, folio 19, column 4, however, understands the "outer Christ of Nazareth" to be meant by "Esau," and consequently understands the children of Esau to be the Christians. It states there:

> “The true Sages have learned through the **Kabbalah** <note>Jewish mystical tradition.</note> that the soul of Esau entered into Jesus of Nazareth, and that he therefore dwelled in the wilderness and was a man of the field; he was also a man of quarrel and strife with the Sages of the **Pharisees**. And perhaps he is called **Yeshua** <note>original: "ישוע Jeschua," the Hebrew name for Jesus.</note> for this reason, because the letters of this name are the very same letters of the name **Esau** <note>original: "עשו Esau."</note>, if Esau is written fully—namely, with the addition of the letter **Yod**. For this reason, all those who accept his law and faith and serve him are called children of **Edom** <note>In rabbinic literature, Edom (another name for Esau) became a frequent code-word for the Roman Empire and, later, the Christian Church.</note>, because Jesus is Esau, and Esau is Edom.”

This Jesus is the "literal Jesus" in the New Testament, appearing as the **Clergy-Christ** <note>original: "Pfaffen-Christus." The term "Pfaffe" was often used by mystical or radical groups to mock the institutionalized, professional priesthood.</note>, and the clergy were themselves this Jesus in their teaching. They were the "man in the wilderness" of dead, literalist doctrines: the arch-quarreler with the Pharisees (which means "separated teachers"), who were separated from their clerical faith—that is, with Jews, Turks <note>A contemporary term for Muslims.</note>, and Heathens. Esau is actually the Old Testament, and Jacob is the New Testament. Because the Old Testament in its literal sense points to Jesus of Nazareth—namely, one literal teaching pointing to another—and because the Old Testament lost its life and rule when the New Testament arrived, yet the "literal Christ" gained dominion; it is therefore said that the soul of Esau entered into Jesus of Nazareth, and that this Jesus was Esau. The Christians, however, who accepted the clerical law and clerical teaching from the letter of the New Testament, would be the children of Edom, or the Edomites.

The Christ of the Christians is thus the Esau who has no blessing and who has no part in the Kingdom of Christ as the world to come, for now this idol is being rooted out (Daniel 9:26). Here one can rightly see how the Spirit of God speaks in parables and comparisons of one thing against another, and how He interchanges the images. For when compared to the outer Christ, the teachers of other religions are the Pharisees. Compared to the true Jesus Christ...

### Those who Mock the Rabbis shall go to Hell.

For we occasionally find something they have said, the meaning and intent of which our intellect is unable to grasp, because it is too meager, and because such things are sometimes contrary to reason and contrary to nature. Therefore, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, have said that whoever makes a mockery of such things shall be punished for it and journey to Hell."

See *Menorath Hammaor* <note>original: "The Candelabra of Light," a popular 14th-century ethical work by Isaac Aboab.</note>, folio 12, column 4, Title, "The Second Lamp," "First General Rule," "Second Part," chapter 2. Since one now knows who has mocked the Rabbis so greatly, one also knows who specifically shall go to Hell.

### Israel is Free from Hell.

The Talmud, Tractate *Eruvin* <note>A tractate concerning the laws of the Sabbath boundary.</note>, folio 19, column 1, says: Resh Lakish <note>A prominent 3rd-century scholar of the Land of Israel.</note> says: The fire of Hell has no power over the sinners in Israel. ## The Nature of the Punishments of Hell.

§. 26. <term>Rabbi Bahya</term> <note>original: "R. Bechai," referring to Bahya ben Asher, a famous 13th-century Spanish Jewish commentator.</note> on the Five Books of Moses, folio 171, column 3, in the <term>Portion of Korah</term> <note>original: "Parascha korah," the section of the Torah dealing with the rebellion of Korah.</note>, on the words of Psalm 9:17 <note>The author uses the older numbering, Psalm 9, 18.</note>, *The wicked shall be turned into hell*, says thus:

But because David says: <term>Yashuvu</term> <note>original: "Jaschufu."</note>, <gloss>they shall return</gloss>, and does not say <term>Yeredu</term> <note>original: "jerudu."</note>, <gloss>they shall go down</gloss>, this indicates the severity of the punishments, which have no end: for after they have been consumed in the fire of Hell, they return, or come back, and are made anew, as from the beginning, so that they may be consumed by the fire once more: and so it goes with them alternately from generation to generation, and this is the meaning of the word ישובו <gloss>they shall return</gloss> <note>Hebrew: *Yashuvu*.</note>. I have also seen in the <term>Midrash</term> <note>A collection of ancient Jewish interpretations of the Bible.</note> on the Order of the World, or <term>Seder Olam</term>, that <term>Sheol</term> <note>The Hebrew term for the underworld or the grave.</note> is the seventh dwelling of Hell, half of which is fire and the other half is hail: and there, the wicked jump from the fire into the hail, and from the hail into the fire, and the angel of Hell drives them, as a shepherd drives his flock, from the mountain to a hill, and from the hill to the mountain, as it is said in Psalm 49:14: *They lie in hell like sheep; death shall feed on them.*"

See also <term>Nishmat Hayyim</term> <note>"The Breath of Life," a work on the soul by Menasseh Ben Israel (1651).</note>, folio 38, column 2, chapter 14, Discourse 1. Also, <term>Toldot Yitzhak</term> <note>"Generations of Isaac," a commentary by Isaac Caro.</note>, folio 90, column 2, in the Portion of Korah. Also, <term>Reshit Hokhmah</term> <note>"The Beginning of Wisdom," a popular 16th-century Kabbalistic ethical manual.</note>, folio 47, column 2, chapter 12, titled <term>The Gate of Fear</term> <note>original: "Schaar hajirah."</note>.

The lower Hell of this time in the outward teaching is described here, and within this, the "Order of the World" along with the great mystery of the actual Hell is simultaneously indicated.

## The Nature of the Punishments of Hell.

§. 26. <term>Rabbi Bahya</term> <note>Rabbi Bahya ben Asher, a famous 13th-century Spanish commentator and Kabbalist.</note> in his commentary on the Five Books of Moses, folio 171, column 3, in the <term>Parashat Korah</term> <note>The weekly Torah portion covering Numbers 16:1–18:32, which deals with Korah's rebellion and his being swallowed by the earth.</note>, regarding the words of Psalm 9:18 <note>In many English Bibles, this is Psalm 9:17: "The wicked shall be turned into hell."</note>, "The wicked must return to hell," says the following:

> "Our Rabbis, of blessed memory, have interpreted this as referring to the lowest chamber of hell. But because David says: *Jashufu* <note>Hebrew: יָשׁוּבוּ; "they shall return."</note>, they must return, and does not say *jerudu* <note>Hebrew: יֵרְדוּ; "they shall go down."</note>, they must go down, this indicates the severity of the punishments which have no end. I have also seen in the <term>Midrash</term> <note>A genre of Rabbinic literature that interprets biblical texts through stories and homilies.</note> regarding the 'Order of the World' or *Seder Olam*, that <term>Sheol</term> <note>The biblical term for the place of the dead.</note> is the seventh dwelling of hell, half of which is fire and the other half hail. And there the wicked leap from the fire into the hail, and from the hail into the fire, and the Angel of Hell drives them as a shepherd drives his flock, from the mountain to a hill, and from the hill to the mountain, as it is said in Psalm 49:15 <note>Psalm 49:14 in English Bibles.</note>: 'They lie in hell like sheep; death shall feed on them.'"

See also *Nishmat Hayyim* <note>“The Breath of Life,” a work on the soul by Menasseh ben Israel (1651).</note>, folio 38, column 2, chapter 14, Treatise I. The Tractate <term>Berachoth</term>, folio 43, column 2, says: It is better for a man to throw himself into a fiery furnace than to publicly put his neighbor to shame, as this Sammael and his like have done to the Jews. These things fit very well here.

## How the Wicked Sometimes Have Some Rest in Hell.

§. 34. This refers to the Hell of this present time within the outer Church, and by no means to the state after death. The wicked have one and a half hours of rest during each morning, evening, and night prayer. The morning, evening, and night prayers are the three religions of the Jews, Christians, and Muslims; for these emerged from a preceding doctrine or Hell, and they believed they had now found their redemption in their own. Thus, this merely illustrates how they have rested in their outward matters of faith.

### How the Wicked Sometimes Have Some Rest in Hell.

§. 34. This refers to the Hell of this present time within the outer Church, and by no means to the state after death. <term>Jalkut Reubeni</term> <note>A 17th-century Kabbalistic collection by Reuben Hoschke.</note>, fol. 167. col. 4. <term>Parashat Va'etchanan</term> from the <term>Zohar</term>, <term>Parashat Noach</term>, says of this as follows:

In all three administrations, God also had mercy on the pious three times. Within this mercy and resting, there is always one and a half hours. The one hour is the "Outer," and the half-hour is the "Inner" which was present alongside the Outer, and in which the pious rested and God had mercy on them. One must therefore only pay attention to the comparisons, and everything will be found.

*Jalkut Chadash*, folio 163, column 4, number 3, under the title *Shabbat*, says: Those who enjoyed any rest on the Sabbath always had to endure double punishment on Friday. Friday, as the last day of the week, signifies the end of the outer Church, where judgment is passed upon outer idolatries, and in that process they certainly receive double punishment.

### How Deliverance from Hell Occurs Through the Kaddish Prayer.

§. 38. The prayers of the Jews were fashioned by God Himself and, in their true sense, refer to the time of deliverance mentioned in the *Revelation of Christ* <note>original: "Off. C." — likely referring to a specific mystical commentary or a section of the author's own "Revelations."</note>. Until now, they were sealed and could not be prayed in their true sense. > Praised be God, who is glorious, from eternity to eternity. Praised be You, Lord our God, King of the world, who has chosen us from all nations and has given us Your law, the true sense of Your word!

## How Redemption from Hell occurs through the Kaddish Prayer.

§. 38. The prayers of the Jews were composed by God Himself and, in their true sense, pertain to the time of redemption in the Revelation of the Eternal Gospel <note>original: "Off. C." — likely *Offenbarung des Ewigen Evangeliums* (Revelation of the Eternal Gospel), a text often cited in Radical Pietist circles.</note>. Until now, they were sealed and could not be prayed in their true sense. But now, since the true meaning has been unlocked and they can be prayed rightly, redemption also comes from the Hell of this age and of the external doctrine. The <term>Kaddish</term> <note>original: "Kadesch" — the Jewish prayer of sanctification, often associated with mourning and the elevation of souls.</note> prayer reads as follows: The great name of God, Jesus Christ, our father Adam, must be sanctified, and according to his will, the world shall be governed, as all peoples shall become one in his revelation. He, the <term>Messiah</term>, shall administer his kingdom during their life and our life, and during the life of the house of <term>Israel</term>, before the Father who is in heaven. To this the congregation responds: Amen! May the great name be praised for all eternity. The cantor sings these words loudly, and thereafter the congregation responds: You shall praise, so that God may be praised, adorned, exalted, and made glorious. Exalted and praised be the holy name of God! Praised be He, even beyond every <term>benediction</term> <note>original: "Benedeyung" — blessing or song of praise.</note>, song, praise, and honor that we may utter to Him in this world. Amen. Thereupon the cantor addresses the angels, as it were, and says: Receive the plea and the prayer of all <term>Israel</term> before their Father who is in heaven. Amen. May great peace and praise descend from heaven upon us and upon all <term>Israel</term>, Amen. See <term>Nishmat Hayyim</term> <note>original: "Nischmath Chajim" — *The Breath of Life* by Menasseh ben Israel (1651).</note>, folio 90, column 1.

In the same way, redemption from Hell shall come through the prayer <term>Krias Shema</term> <note>original: "Kesrias Schema" — the recitation of the Shema, the central declaration of Jewish faith.</note>, which reads: God, our father Adam, is a true King. Hear, <term>Israel</term>, the Lord our God is one God. Blessed be the name, the glory of His kingdom, forever and ever. When this prayer is prayed by the whole <term>Israel</term> of believers from all nations, then the three gods of the Christians are buried <note>A radical critique of the Trinity, suggesting that traditional Nicene theology is a form of spiritual "Hell" or external bondage from which the believer must be freed.</note>, and we are redeemed from the Hell of the external church.

Particularly, however, the redemption from Hell shall occur through the prayer "Bless the Lord" <note>original: "ברכו את ה׳" (Barechu et Hashem) — the call to prayer.</note>, which reads: Praise God, who is glorious! This is said by the cantor, to which the congregation responds: Praised be God, who is glorious, from eternity to eternity. Praised be You, Lord our God, King of the world, who has chosen us from all peoples and has given us Your law, the true sense of Your word!

# Of Hell and Purgatory.

...have more than enough endured. This reconciliation I have set forth in the treatise, **Reconciliation of Israel**, just as is said here, and so God Himself gives me testimony in these discourses that I have done it rightly, and in His spirit, impulse, and will.

> **Rabbi Akiva**, in **Othioth** <note>original: "Othioth" — referring to *Otiot de-Rabbi Akiva*, an ancient midrashic text that provides mystical interpretations of the Hebrew alphabet.</note>, folio 15, column 4, folio 16, column 1, says: "The wicked would in the future be redeemed from Hell if they said **Amen**. Through the saying of this **Amen**, the whole world would be moved, and their voice would be heard by God. When such happens, inquiry is made on their behalf, and God then has mercy on them, giving the angels **Michael** and **Gabriel** the keys to Hell. These would then open the 40,000 gates of the same, according to **Isaiah** 26:2, and bring them out. Afterward, they would wipe the redeemed clean, anointing and healing them from the wounds of Hell, dressing them in pure garments, taking them by the hand, and leading them to God and to the righteous, according to **2 Chronicles** 6:41."

The word **Amen** is the essential truth in the true sense of the Word of God, through which the whole world is moved. When people carry this in their hearts and mouths, they are redeemed from the Hell of this current age and from external doctrine, and God hears their voice and has mercy on them. **Michael** and **Gabriel** represent the spirit of the two Testaments in their true sense, which is found in **Elijah** or the **Messiah**. This one has the keys to Hell and to Heaven, **Isaiah** 22:22, **Revelation** 3:7, **Matthew** 16:19. The 40,000 gates of Hell are all the external doctrines of the Word of God, which he shuts out. Through this, the bonds of the "Hell of the Letter" <note>A common Pietist concept where literal, non-spiritual interpretation of the Bible is viewed as a spiritual prison or "hell."</note> are loosed, and the true doctrine is opened, of which **Isaiah** says in the cited place: Open the gates, that the righteous nation which keeps the faith may enter in. He leads **Israel** out from the <term>priest-teaching</term> <note>original: "Pfaffen-Lehre" — a derogatory term used by Radical Pietists to describe the professional, institutional clergy whom they viewed as corrupt and spiritually blind.</note>, wipes them clean of the priestly filth, anoints and heals them with the true doctrine, and dresses them in this as in pure garments. He takes them by the hand therein and leads them to God and to the righteous, according to **2 Chronicles** 6:41, where it says: Now therefore arise, **Jehovah Elohim**, into Thy rest, Thou and the Ark of Thy strength—which is the doctrine of the <term>New Covenant</term> <note>original: "O. C." — likely an abbreviation for *Oeconomia Christi* (The Dispensation of Christ) or a similar term for the spiritual Order of the New Covenant.</note>. Let Thy priests, O **Jehovah Elohim**, be clothed with salvation, and let Thy saints rejoice in goodness. Here the **Amen**, as the truth, shall fill the whole earth, and all lies shall be bound with their father, the devil. That is the redemption from the Hell of this current age.

# Chapter 6.
## Of Death and the Angel of Death.

->§. 1.<-

According to the teaching of the Rabbis, all who die are slain by the <term>Malach hammoves</term> <note>Hebrew: מלאך המות, the Angel of Death</note>. However, they teach of two Angels of Death. One is said to be a holy angel, namely Gabriel; the other is an evil angel, whom they call Sammael. According to *Maimon* <note>Moses Maimonides, the preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher.</note> in *The Guide for the Perplexed* <note>original Latin/Hebrew: *More nevochim*, Part II, chapter 30, folio 77, column 1.</note>, and in the commentary upon it by *Rabbi Shem Tov*, this angel is said to be the Devil, because he misleads man from the good path onto the evil one.

The booklet *The Good of the Land* <note>original: *Tuf haarez* (Tuv Ha'Aretz)</note> says on folio 16, column 3: "He who dies in the Land of Israel does not die by the Angel of Death, but by a holy angel." And on folio 31, column 4, it is taught extensively:

> "That the angel Sammael is placed over those dead who die outside the Land of Israel. The angel Gabriel, however, is over those who die within it. Both angels stand under <term>Metatron</term> <note>In Jewish mysticism, a high-ranking angel who serves as the celestial scribe or mediator.</note> as servants. They do not take away the souls of men themselves, but have many angels under them, of whom each is set over only one person to take his soul from him. When this has happened, these angels pass away and no longer exist, as each one is created for only a single soul."

See also the *Yalkut Reuveni* <note>original: *Jalkut rubeni*</note>, section 13, title: *Metatron*. Also, the *New Yalkut* <note>original: *Jalkut chadasch*</note>, folio 31, columns 3 and 4, number 44, from the *Zohar*. Also, the *Chain of Tradition* <note>original: *Schalscheleth hakkabala*</note>, folio 68, column 2.

These things must be understood both in terms of nature and in terms of doctrine. In nature, the satanic nature—which is spread around the whole earth and up to the firmament of the clouds—is the Devil and Sammael, the Angel of Death, who has killed all men until now. This Sammael, however, has many angels or evil spirits under him; namely, "small forms," just as Sammael is the "great form." Every person has such an evil angel who is formed with him, and who also dies and passes away with him, as I have already mentioned in the *Book of the World*, and as is expressly stated here. Note the reason for this! # Of Death and the Angel of Death.

> “When the dogs howl, the Angel of Death is coming into the city: but when the dogs play or mock, then Elijah is coming into the city.” <note>This is a well-known passage from the Babylonian Talmud, Tractate Bava Kamma 60b, reflecting folk beliefs about animals sensing the supernatural.</note>

The Angel of Death is the final Antichrist, and his new teaching is the pestilence. The City, however, is the external Christian church and its doctrine, and the dogs are the priests of the Christians. When the Angel of Death comes with his insidious mouse-teaching <note>original: "Mäusins-Lehre." This likely refers to a "vermin-like" or corrupting doctrine that spreads quietly like the plague, which was often associated with mice/rats.</note>; then there is a hunger or a famine for the Word of God in the church, and also the pestilence. At that time, let no one go out into the external teachings of the church, and one must be careful not to defend them or to encounter the Antichrist therein: for he has the power to strike all of that down, along with all the people who wish to remain clinging to the external teachings. One should shut oneself inside the true teaching of the <term>Off. C.</term> <note>Abbreviation for "Offenbarung Christi" (Revelation of Christ), likely the title of the specific mystical text the author is promoting.</note>. Whoever encounters him in the external teaching and tries to contradict him will be harmed and brings the guilt upon himself. Hitherto, Elijah has been in the city, ever since the <term>Revelation of Christ</term> was first published; but the dogs—the Satanic priests—have only mocked and laughed at it. But when the Angel of Death appears publicly, then these dogs will howl. These are the ones of whom it is written: *Outside are the dogs, and the sorcerers, and the whoremongers, and the murderers, and the idolaters, and everyone who loves and practices a lie,* Revelation 22:15. And these six types are all the priests of the Christian church in their six ages from the beginning until their current end (excepting the very few pious ones, of whom one finds scarcely one among a thousand). This pronouncement will be offensive to you Christians, but you shall experience it. For these "priest-dogs" are to blame for the fact that the <term>Revelation of Christ</term> cannot go out publicly to all people, even though it has been sent out at great expense to most lands of Christendom since 1770. Thus, it will become known to you all too late, for which your priests are to blame, and then you may vomit them out.

When the Angel of Death comes as the Antichrist, then the Angel of Death will also come in nature, with hunger and pestilence, about which all your priests could tell you nothing; for the dogs themselves know nothing and understand nothing of God's Word, and have thus only blinded you and led you into error in exchange for the bread they have devoured from you.

# Of Death and the Angel of Death.

...as it is in the teaching, so it is also with the Angel of Death in nature, who is also present here at the same time. When a godless man dies—especially a **depraved priest** <note>original: *Laster-Pfaff*; a highly derogatory term used by radical reformers to describe clergy they viewed as corrupt or immoral</note>—his evil angel stands by him, pours out the poison of death for him, and takes his soul to himself, leading it into Hell. For just as this angel was his chief leader during his life, so he is also his leader in death. And this evil angel of his never leaves him; he remains with him until that nature in which he is held in Hell comes to an end and he is redeemed from Hell. <note>This suggests a belief in a temporary or "purgatorial" Hell rather than eternal damnation, where a soul stays until its "nature" is purified.</note> It is exactly the same with every other nature of the external world. As long as a man remains in any of those natures, he also keeps an angel from that same nature who belongs to him.

This sermon will greatly displease **Sammael** <note>In Jewish tradition, Sammael is the Accuser or Angel of Death; here, the author uses the name to address an opponent or the spirit of the institutional church</note> when he reads it or hears of it from his brothers, but that is of no consequence. **Haman** must hang, along with his sons, on the very same gallows that he had erected for the pious and innocent Jewish people. <note>A reference to the Book of Esther, symbolizing how those who persecute the "true" believers will suffer the fate they intended for others.</note> Let the **hostile birds**—the brothers of Sammael and Haman—see their own reflection in this; for the Angel of Death is an undaunted hero. He leads the **priest-angel** with great force and mercilessness into his tent. This is what I say to you, you hostile birds.

# THE LODGE'S ASSISTANCE FUND IS NOTHING BUT 
# THE PHILANTHROPY OF THE BRETHREN.
# (FOUNDER: DR. AUGUSTIN)

If the lodge is dissolved or ceases to exist, the assistance fund shall be used for the benefit of the poor in Berlin or a similar charitable institution in this city; the choice of the recipient shall be made by the majority of the lodge or its representatives or liquidators. In no case shall the sum be distributed among the lodge members or their heirs.

The administrators of the foundation are the Master of the Chair <term>Master of the Chair: The elected presiding officer of a Masonic lodge, equivalent to a "Worshipful Master"</term> and the lodge's treasurer, who are obligated to safeguard the fund and utilize the interest. They are required to keep accounts of the administration. The capital shall be invested in secure securities.

According to the wording of the decree of July 18, 1840, the value amounts to 400 <term>Thalers: A large silver coin used as a standard currency in German states before the unification of the Empire</term> with 100 Thalers in interest.

---

## OF LEGACIES

Unless otherwise ordered, any legacy <note>Referring here to a "Vermächtniss" or a gift left in a will</note> flows into the capital of the Assistance Fund.
(Draft statutes of 1845, § 2).

---

## OF THE FOUNDING ANNIVERSARY

The annual celebration of the founding day is to take place at the lodge; the date is always determined by the Master of the Chair.
Should the lodge at any time be unable to organize a celebration due to a lack of means, it must nevertheless remember the deceased brethren on this day.

---

## OF MEMBERSHIP DUES

The lodge must maintain a regular membership; all brethren are to pay their contribution according to the legal provisions of the federal constitution <note>original: "Bundesordnung," referring to the governing rules of the larger Masonic Grand Lodge or union to which this local lodge belongs</note>.
